title: 散户投资者并未完全放弃人工智能交易，但他们似乎更加谨慎
content:
Retail investors aren't giving up on the artificial intelligence trade. But they are getting selective and adding downside protection as markets head into the fall.

Investors are using put options and inverse ETFs to hedge risk while still positioning for upside in individual technology stocks, according to data from Vanda Research and Charles Schwab. Put options give the holder the right to sell an asset at a stated price by a certain date. Inverse ETFs aim to move in the opposite direction from the index they're following.

"Retail investors are selectively trading in the classic AI theme but also adding downside protection via options and inverse ETFs," Vanda's global equity strategist Kaidi Meng told CNBC in an emailed statement.

Retail flows look very different now compared with prior years, Meng said. "Previously, retail bought any major dips almost without question. However, this year, we are seeing a more selective retail investor that is either switching between stocks quickly or buying underlying stocks while also buying protective puts," she added.

​Since April, Meng said put buying of the top 12 retail-favored stocks in 2026 has almost doubled versus the first quarter, despite an overall reduction in cash purchases of stocks. Put buying went up to 110% from about 26% of net cash buying, even as outright stock purchases have declined. Net cash buying refers to the amount investors spend on purchasing assets versus the amount they sell.

The strategist said growth of ETF strategies, including levered vehicles, has led to a different kind of risk-taking appetite from retail cohorts. "Flows into ETFs signal a trend of reduced outright exposure, rather than just an uptick in downside hedges," Meng said.

Vanda's data shows that since mid-April, buying of both bullish and bearish tech ETFs, including leveraged funds, has declined. Bullish activity fell sharply, down about 50%, Meng pointed out, compared with a roughly 35% decline for bearish ETFs.

Overall, Meng said retail investors appear to be adding downside protection through puts on individual stocks and inverse ETFs for broader market exposure, while also cutting their long positions.

"This reduction in long exposure may be a function of broader profit-taking after years of successful buy-the-dip strategies, or this could be a sign of retail investors choosing to take increased risk via more speculative stocks, levered ETFs, and betting sites," she said.

The increased demand for protection, however, doesn't mean retail investors have broadly turned bearish.

Data from Charles Schwab show that many investors are still buying and positioning for further upside. Schwab investors continued to buy in July despite a choppy market backdrop, lifting theSchwab Trading Activity Index, known as STAX, for a third straight month and bringing it to its highest level since January 2022.

The index rose to 59.80 in July from 59.12 in June. Schwab clients remained net buyers, with the brokerage firm seeing more than two buyers for every seller in July.

Arecent report by the firm showedthat as many tech stocks pulled back, traders appeared more willing to buy dips in names with sharper moves, while showing less interest in stocks that remained rangebound. Notably, Nvidia, which was regularly among the top five names in STAX, was absent from those rankings in July.

Joe Mazzola, Schwab's head trading and derivatives strategist, told CNBC the firm saw a modest pickup in put buying on theInvesco QQQ Trust (QQQ)during the week of Aug. 7.

Mazzola said Schwab investors were continuing to sell puts on individual AI-linked stocks such asNvidia,MicronandSandisk, taking advantage of elevated option premiums, while buying lower-cost QQQ puts to hedge some of their broader tech exposure.

But he said while the hedging pickup is noticeable, it is not dramatic.

"Put selling and call buying, so they're trying to position themselves for an additional rally," he said. A call option gives the investor the right to buy a stock at a specified price by a certain date.

Inverse and leveraged ETFs can be used to hedge risk, but traders can also use them to make directional bets.

"Many advanced investors continuously evaluate both market opportunities and portfolio risk, adjusting exposures and strategies as market conditions, investment themes, and their own objectives evolve," Bryan Koplin, head of advanced trading at Fidelity Investments told CNBC in an email.

For example, some may use options or other advanced strategies to help manage portfolio risk or express a market view based on expected price movements.

"Similarly, we're also seeing continued interest in leveraged and inverse ETFs," Koplin said. "While these products could be viewed as portfolio hedging, they are frequently used by active traders to make directional bets on expected market movements."

According to Koplin, their ease of use can make them an attractive alternative to strategies involving margin borrowing or short selling.

But he also warns that investors should carefully consider the objectives, risks and generally short-term nature of these products before trading them.

"As advanced investors evaluate portfolio construction, risk management, and more sophisticated trading strategies," Koplin said, "access to education, research, and customizable tools can play an important role in helping them make tailored, informed decisions and navigate evolving market opportunities."

title: 汽车经销商越来越依赖零部件和服务来获取利润
content:
When people buy new cars, auto dealerships make money. When they don't, dealerships still find a way to make money.

A dealership typically has four profit streams: new vehicle sales, used vehicle sales, parts and service departments, and finance and insurance offices. This gives dealers some kind of product or service to offer in good times and bad.

Now, parts and service departments and finance and insurance packages are becoming more important sources of profit for car dealers, as profits from new vehicle sales show signs of softening.

"The auto retailer remains one of the more attractive hedged business models," said Erin Kerrigan, founder and managing director of Kerrigan Advisors, a sell-side advisory and consulting firm for dealerships.

"If you lose $10 of new vehicle revenue, you only have to pick up $1 of service to have your gross margin remain flat," she said. "It's 5% new car margin, 50% service margin."

This is why dealerships were still profitable even in the financial crisis, while automakers such asGeneral Motorsand Chrysler, now part ofStellantis, went bankrupt, she added.

During the pandemic,new car pricessoared, due in large part to tight supply. The average pretax profit per dealership more than tripled from $1.9 million in 2018 to $6.8 million in 2022, according to a Kerrigan Advisors analysis of publicly traded dealership group filings.

Facing supply constraints, automakers manufactured more expensive and higher-margin vehicles. That trend has continued for years, but is starting to show signs of buckling.

"If you look at the weakest part of auto sales right now, it's what we call the mass affluent," said Jeff Lick, managing director at Stephens. "Those are the people that generally go off and lease the high-end Lexus. Everyone talks about the K-shaped economy in the car business. You're actually seeing relative strength in the lower part of the K, because that's the need. The mid-level [BMW] 5 Series, that's the want. And you know, that consumption can be postponed."

Since that 2022 peak, average gross profits for dealerships owned by the public dealership groups fell to about $3.9 million in 2025, according to Kerrigan Advisors.

But over roughly the same period, the average dealership's parts and service gross profit rose — from $3.3 million in 2020 to $5 million in 2025, according to Kerrigan Advisors.

Finance and insurance, often abbreviated to F&I, often contributes an outsized share of gross profit compared with revenue. Finance and insurance revenues forAsbury Automotive, one of six publicly tradeddealership groups, was only about 4% of revenues from January to June, according to the company. But it made up 23% of the company's gross profit.

"F&I has proved very stable, if not continued to grow slightly," said Glenn Chin, senior equity analyst at Seaport Research Partners. "I do think there's true value in some of these products, as much as people poo poo them. If you're spending $50,000 on a new car, a lot of people don't feel comfortable leaving that fully exposed. So they will buy a bumper to bumper warranty or they will buy a prepaid maintenance plan."

Because dealerships are just conduits for these contracts, that transaction is almost pure profit, he added.

There is a potential challenge to this. While service revenues and profits might be up in raw numbers, dealers are getting a smaller share of the pie.

A Cox Automotive report from April found dealer share of service visits dropped from 33% in 2017 to 29% in 2025.

Another 2026 report, by global consulting and merger and acquisition advisory firm Ducker Carlisle, found that from 2020 to 2025, the share of customers who considered chain service centers, such as Jiffy Lube, Meineke andWalmart, their "primary" service provider grew from 20% to 42%.

"A 22-point swing in five years does not happen by chance, particularly because the trend has been regular and consistent," the report said.

There is a perception among consumers that dealers charge more for service than independent repair shops and chains, although some auto industry groups say the evidence supports the opposite, according to Cox Automotive. The group said the average consumer spend for parts at a dealer was $261, versus $275 at a general repair shop.

"The franchise dealers have come to realize the importance of service and parts," Chin said. "They are taking great effort to dispel that notion and try to become more competitive on pricing. They have all grown mid-single digits since Covid. Part of that is due to elevated warranty and recalls, but also because of their efforts to become more competitive."

title: 每周抵押贷款需求随着利率的上升而停滞，但利率现在再次走高。
content:
上周抵押贷款利率没有变化，使得购房者或现有房主几乎没有动力打电话给贷方。

抵押贷款申请总量与前一周基本持平，根据抵押贷款银行家协会的季节性调整指数，下降了 0.4%。

贷款余额符合要求的 30 年期固定利率抵押贷款的平均合同利率， 832,750 美元或以下，保持在 6.77% 不变，对于首付 20% 的贷款，积分从 0.67 下降到 0.65，包括启动费。

住房贷款再融资申请本周增加了 2%，比一年前同一周下降了 18%，当时利率略低。

“上周抵押贷款利率和申请变化不大，仅传统贷款和 VA 贷款的再融资略有增加，而联邦住房管理局的再融资则较低，”MBA 副总裁兼副首席经济学家乔尔·坎 (Joel Kan) 在一份新闻稿中表示。 “贷款规模较大的借款人仍然不太可能以较高水平的利率进行再融资。再融资的平均贷款规模继续缩小，上周降至 282,200 美元，为 2025 年 6 月以来的最低水平。”

CNBC 的戴安娜·奥利克 (Diana Olick) 的《房地产游戏》为房地产投资者提供了新的和不断变化的机会，每周发送到您的收件箱。

在此订阅以获取访问权限今天。

本周，购房抵押贷款申请量下降了 2%，比一年前同一周下降了 3%。虽然抵押贷款利率上周没有变化，但一直徘徊在最新区间的较高端。

“除了经济不确定性之外，鉴于抵押贷款利率上升对每月抵押贷款付款的影响，负担能力困难再次成为购房者推迟购买决定的一个原因，”菅直人补充道。

根据《抵押新闻日报》的另一项调查，抵押贷款利率从本周开始再次小幅走高。

title: 由于销售反弹和巨额关税退款提高了利润，目标展望上调
content:
Targeton 周三公布了季度收益，受到关税退款的推动，并提高了全年指引，因为该零售商显示出更多迹象表明其扭亏为盈。

该公司表示，净销售额较上年增长 5.3%。根据 StreetAccount 的数据，可比销售额增长 3.8%，高于华尔街预期的 2.4%。塔吉特在其新闻稿中补充说，它看到了各个类别的“广泛”实力。

“我们对迄今为止取得的进展感到鼓舞，而且我们也对未来的重要工作有清醒的认识，”首席执行官迈克尔·菲德尔克(Michael Fiddelke)在接受记者电话采访时表示。 “第二季度是我们今年早些时候制定的为塔吉特开启增长新篇章的计划中向前迈出的重要一步。本季度我们所看到的情况反映了我们知道实施战略所需的变革水平。”

塔吉特第二季度业绩还包括关税退款带来的净利润增加 7.52 亿美元，即每股 1.65 美元。该公司表示，其第二季度毛利率和营业收入包括该还款带来的 9.94 亿美元税前收益。

Target 上调了整个财年的预期，原因是销售趋势更加强劲，而且利润也一度得到提升。该零售商将全年净销售增长指引上调至 5% 左右，提高了 1 个百分点。

预计全年每股收益（包括关税退款）将在 9.90 美元至 10.90 美元之间。不包括还款在内，该范围将为每股 8.25 美元至 9.25 美元，而之前的预期为每股 7.50 美元至 8.50 美元。

虽然 Target 连续两个季度公布了令人鼓舞的业绩，但 Fiddelke 表示，他对公司的扭亏为盈仍持谨慎态度。

“需要明确的是，我们还有很多工作要做，”他告诉记者。 “更强的执行力和更好的顾客反馈相结合，为我们继续推进我们的战略奠定了坚实的基础。”

尽管取得了这样的业绩，塔吉特股价在盘前交易中仍下跌了约 4%。

根据 LSEG 对分析师的调查，该零售商公布的第二财季财报与华尔街的预期相比如下：

截至 8 月 1 日的三个月期间，塔吉特报告的净利润为18.8 亿美元，即每股 4.11 美元，而上年同期为 9.35 亿美元，即每股 2.05 美元。这一比较包括塔吉特公司从收取关税退款中获得的收益。

“两个强劲的季度并不是目标，”菲德尔克告诉记者。 “随着时间的推移，持续、持久的收入和利润增长是我们所追求的。”

该公司表示，本季度数字可比销售额增长了 8.7%，当日送达增长超过 25%。

该公司表示，随着其所有六个主要类别的增长，其食品和美容业务表现强劲。然而，其服装和家居品类落后于其他细分市场，这一差异公司高管表示，他们打算解决这一问题。

“我们知道像家居这样的品类将是一个多年的旅程，我们对客人的反应感到鼓舞，我们已经在家居这样的品类中做出了改变，”菲德尔克告诉记者。 “我们改变了 75% 的装饰配件品种，并且我们看到了强劲的[可比销售额]跟随这一变化。坦率地说，我们需要在这两个类别中进行更多此类改进。”

Target 还表示，它已经降低了 10,000 多种商品的价格，并减少了更多库存，以努力让顾客重返其商店。 第二季度开设了 17 家新店。

该公司一直在努力向投资者证明，它正走在恢复持续增长和重新吸引核心客户的正确道路上。由于宏观经济状况的压力，许多消费者继续减少支出，因此盈利得以实现。

上个季度，Target 报告五个季度以来首次出现正同店销售数据，增长 5.6%。

Target 的股价今年上涨了 55% 以上。

title: Lowe’s 因家居装修支出面临“压力”，前景黯淡
content:
劳森周三公布的业绩好坏参半，因为这家家居装修零售商表示，它看到了项目支出的“压力”。

尽管该公司没有下调全年指导，但将其前景更新为之前指导的下限。目前预计总销售额为 920 亿美元，而之前为 920 亿至 940 亿美元，可比销售额将持平，而持平则增长 2%。预计全年调整后每股收益为 12.25 美元，而此前为 12.25 至 12.75 美元。

Lowe's 股价在盘前交易中下跌约 2%。

根据 LSEG 对分析师的调查，该公司第二财季的表现与华尔街的预期相比如下：

Lowe's 本季度净利润为 2.4 美元十亿美元，即每股 4.27 美元，与去年同期大致相同。排除一次性因素并包括关税退款福利，该公司报告调整后每股收益为 4.40 美元。

Lowe's 还表示，关税退款使其本季度每股收益增加了 11 美分。

该公司报告本季度总销售额为 259.6 亿美元，高于上年同期的 239.6 亿美元。据该公司称，可比销售额增长了 0.2%，部分原因是其专业服务和家庭服务销售表现强劲。

Lowe's 的在线销售额也增长了 15.7%，不过该公司补充称，这一业绩部分被 DIY 客户的宏观经济压力所抵消。

“虽然近期仍然充满活力，但我们的团队正在高水平执行，推进我们的 Total Home 战略并进行投资，以推动增长和盈利。”首席执行官马文·埃里森(Marvin Ellison)在一份声明中表示。

该家居装修零售商正在努力应对房地产市场放缓和消费者更加谨慎的问题。

Lowe的竞争对手家得宝(Home Depot)在周二的收益报告中表示，该公司没有看到客户返回大型项目，并继续在“冻结的房地产市场条件”下运营。

title: 美国禁止英伟达最好的芯片进入中国。现在它正试图堵住一个关键漏洞
content:
Nvidia's effective monopoly over the most powerful chips has made U.S. export controls a key tool in Washington's effort to preserve its advantage over China in the AI race.

But despite U.S. restrictions on exporting the company's most advanced semiconductors, including GB300s, several Chinese firms have reportedly been able to access the chips' compute power via data centers in Southeast Asia.

Less than a week after Moonshot AI released a new model in July, White House official Michael Kratsios accused the company of using Nvidia's GB300 chips via a facility in Thailand.

Moonshot's Kimi K3 is one of a wave of new Chinese AI models that have made leaps in performance in recent months, as the race for AI supremacy between Washington and Beijing intensifies. DeepSeek and Alibaba have also recently released new AI systems that have scored well on performance benchmarks.

Industry watchers say access to advanced compute via overseas cloud providers is a key factor in Chinese AI models gaining capability.U.S. legislation is being discussed to plug this loophole, but hurdles remain before it can have an impact.

Nvidia's most advanced AI chips are under export restrictions to China, though some less capable semiconductors are allowed to be shipped to the country.

Cassia King, senior researcher on the Compute Policy teamat the Institute for AI Policy and Strategy, told CNBC that Moonshot's reported access to compute through a Thai facility was legal "so long as Moonshot isn't actually buying and owning the physical hardware directly."

She said the U.S. export control regime "controls physical AI chips. It does not cover remote access to those chips."

When asked about Chinese firms accessing Nvidia compute overseas to train AI models, a White House official told CNBC: "The Trump administration has implemented the most rigorous export control regime in modern history, and remains committed to safeguarding America's national and economic security."

The U.S. Department of Commerce and Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) did not respond to a request for comment.

Chinese hyperscalers including ByteDance, Alibaba and Tencent have reportedly accessed compute power from Nvidia chips remotely via other Asian nations, including Thailand, Malaysia and Japan. ByteDance and Tencent did not respond to a request for comment. Alibaba declined to comment.

ByteDance was working with Singapore-headquartered Aolani, a cloud provider with Nvidia chips, to access compute in Malaysia, according to a source familiar with the matter, who asked to remain anonymous when discussing private information. The Wall Street Journal first reported the arrangement in March.

Aolani told CNBC it worked "with a global and diversified customer base spanning customers from North America and Asia."

"The companies we service do not have ownership, potential future claim or physical access to the chips that power our solutions," the spokesperson added. "Any permitted access to our services, infrastructure or technology is fully compliant with all applicable regulations."

AI infrastructure buildouts in Southeast Asia are booming as companies look to tap the growing market for advanced compute.

Real estate company JLL estimates that global data center capacity could roughly double to 200GW by 2030.

There are 31 planned 100MW+ data centers across Malaysia, Indonesia and Thailand, compared to just two today, according to data compiled by DC Byte.

Michelle Nie, a visiting fellow in technology and national security at think tank Center for a New American Security, told CNBC that loophole was "threatening U.S. national security."

"The point of chip export controls is to deny China the ability to train frontier AI using advanced U.S. chips," she added.

A proposed piece of legislation, the Remote Access Security Act (RASA), seeks to expand U.S. export controls to include the remote cloud-based access of critical hardware and software. It passed the House of Representatives in January but has yet to pass the Senate.

It faces potential industry pushback, Nie said, adding: "Cloud providers would bear the compliance burden of any KYC and customer verification requirements mandated by the bill."

The passing of RASA alone wouldn't solve the problem, Nie added, saying it would give the U.S. government "the authority to regulate remote access," but it "would still need to create a rule to export-control remote access to advanced chips."

The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) could push through a rule quickly, possibly in a "matter of days" with White House support, said King.

"The challenge will be in making a rule that's effective and enforceable," she added. "Policymakers will need to decide what compute is covered, who should be prohibited from remotely accessing the compute, and how to implement a robust know-your-customer scheme."

title: 竞争对手围剿收购战，全球最大橄榄油公司股价上涨逾15%
content:
周三上午，随着全球最大橄榄油装瓶商和营销商的收购战愈演愈烈，西班牙 Deoleo 的股价上涨超过 15%。

有报道称，西班牙农业食品合作集团 Dcoop 已向 Deoleo 出价 4.7 亿欧元（5.45 亿美元）收购 Deoleo，在包括意大利、法国和澳大利亚在内的跨国收购竞赛中处于领先地位。

西班牙《El Economista》报纸周三援引未透露姓名的知情人士消息称，此次出售尚未最终敲定，但据说目前已进入最后阶段，最初预计于 9 月完成。

如果完成，此次出售将通过创建一个新的橄榄油巨头来巩固西班牙在战略领域的领导地位，该巨头将涵盖一系列品牌，并确保约占全国消费量的 15% 份额。

该报告指出， Dcoop 目前在收购 Deoleo 方面处于领先地位，领先的公司包括意大利公司 Coricelli、Bonifiche Ferraresi 和 Newlat Food、法国公司 Lesieur (Avril) 和澳大利亚 Cobram Estate Olive。

Deoleo 拒绝发表评论。 CNBC 联系 Dcoop 的发言人时，我们未能立即发表评论。

Deoleo 的股价最近上涨 15.7%，创下 52 周新高，有望创下 2022 年 3 月以来的最佳单日表现。

西班牙与意大利和希腊一样，是世界领先的橄榄油生产国之一，也是全球价格的参考。

这种珍贵商品的价格一直在波动。一个季节到另一个季节的变化都非常剧烈，特别是在气候变化、水资源短缺以及病虫害等问题持续存在的情况下。

然而，Bertolli 和 Carbonell 等家用橄榄油品牌的制造商 Deoleo 最近告诉 CNBC，一段前所未有的波动时期已经明确让位于更加稳定的市场条件。

title: 美元风险正在加剧。以下是可能削弱美元的因素
content:
Growing fiscal risks, softer economic data and uncertainty over Federal Reserve policy could intensify pressure on the U.S. dollar, despite recent strength, according to currency strategists.

Higher U.S. bond yields have helped support the dollar in 2026 by attracting more capital inflows into dollar assets.

TheU.S. Dollar Indextracks the performance of the greenback against six major global currencies, including the euro, the pound, the Swiss franc, the Japanese yen and the Canadian dollar. The benchmark is up 1.15% year-to-date, notching a 52-week high of 101.80 on June 24. The index registered at 99.4 as of 5:32 a.m. ET on Wednesday.

Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at Saxo, said higher Treasury yields do not necessarily support the dollar if investors believe the increase reflects fiscal risk, heavier government borrowing or persistent inflation, rather than stronger U.S. growth or tighter Fed policy, said.

The historic relationship between Treasury yields and dollar strength "still matters," Chanana added, but "investors should increasingly ask why U.S. yields are rising."

"A higher yield generated by stronger economic fundamentals is not necessarily equivalent to a higher yield generated by a larger risk premium. That distinction may help explain why higher Treasury yields have recently coexisted with less convincing dollar strength."

Global bonds sold offthis week, with the U.S.30-year Treasury yieldreaching its highest level since 2007. Chanana said any breakdown in the relationship could herald broader portfolio consequences.

"For international investors, U.S. assets have benefited for years from both strong underlying returns and a strong dollar. If that relationship becomes less consistent, geographical diversification may matter more."

Softer U.S. consumption,inflationandemploymentdata have caused investors to reassess expectations for interest rates, and reduce some bullish dollar positions, according to Societe Generale.

The U.S. economy had shown resilience since the start of the Middle East conflict, with Fed rate pricing underpinning the dollar, said Kit Juckes, chief FX strategist at SocGen.

In a note, Juckes said recent weaker inflation and employment prints have since reduced market expectations for higher U.S. rates.

"Long dollar positions are now being cut back in a thin summer market, as the fundamental justification for holding them fades," he said, adding that could potentially drive the dollar index lower, or leave it drifting into an "uninspiring" 95–100 range for the rest of the year.

George Saravelos, global head of FX research at Deutsche Bank, said uncertainty about the Fed's inflation reaction function adds another potential negative for the dollar.

He highlighted "mixed signals" from Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh over the central bank's inflation target and toolkit, adding he views the ambiguity ultimately as dollar-negative.

"We have not boarded the dollar bullish train this year because global growth has been resilient, geopolitical developments pose continuous challenges to dollar dominance and the Fed has been ambivalent on its reaction function to inflation," Saravelos said.

In a note on the recent historic U.S.-Japan intervention tosupport the yen, Saravelos also argued that the Fed's "FIMA" facility ultimately has the same economic impact as quantitative easing.

The Fed's FIMA repo facility allows approved foreign central banks and other monetary authorities to temporarily exchange U.S. Treasury securities for dollars.

"When a foreign government posts treasuries as collateral for cash the Fed prints dollars," Saravelos said. "If the Fed was to sharply increase the size of the FIMA facility in line with the U.S. administration request, we would consider it as an indirect way of Fed monetary financing of UST and an additional dollar negative."

Meanwhile, Elias Haddad, vice president, global head of markets strategy, foreign exchange at BBH, said that a stock market correction may be less of a dollar risk, adding that foreign investors may not abandon dollar assets altogether.

BBH analysis of Treasury data shows foreign purchases of U.S. stocks hit $920 billion in the 12-month period to June, more than triple that for Treasuries, which stood at $294 billion.

"This has led some to argue that the dollar is increasingly vulnerable to an equity market correction, as foreign investors unwind their U.S. stock holdings. We disagree," Haddad said in a note Tuesday. He said a broad stock market sell-off may encourage foreign investors to instead rotate back into safe-haven Treasuries, which he said still underpins the dollar's defensive appeal.

title: Trainline、维珍航空和 RED 驾驶学校因“滴水定价”受到调查
content: 图片来源，Getty Images 图片说明，CMA 表示，顾客应该支付他们看到的价格 作者：Emer Moreau 商业记者发布 2026 年 8 月 19 日，英国夏令时 09:52 更新于 1 小时前Trainline、维珍大西洋航空和 RED Driving School 正在接受消费者监管机构的调查，原因是担心它们没有向顾客提前显示完整价格。竞争与市场管理局 (CMA) 正在调查这三家公司是否从事所谓的“滴注”活动定价”，这是一种非法做法，强制性费用不包含在向客户显示的总体价格中。如果 CMA 认为这些公司违反了法律，可以对其处以罚款或责令他们向客户进行赔偿。Trainline 和维珍航空表示，他们致力于为客户提供透明度，并将与 CMA 充分接触。就 Trainline 而言，CMA 表示，它观察到火车票价中添加的费用高达 2.79 英镑，长途汽车票价的费用高达 1.50 英镑CMA 表示：“对于经常出行的人来说，这两项费用都会增加。”Trainline 此前曾被指控采用滴水定价。铁路和公路办公室表示，2023 年，它和其他六家第三方火车票销售商没有提前告知费用。维珍航空正在接受调查，以确定向购买套餐假期的客户显示的预付费用中是否包含强制性度假费和地方税。 CMA 表示，这些费用各不相同，但可能高达数百英镑，从而大大增加了假期的成本。监管机构正在调查 RED Driving School 是否在向购买驾驶课程的人显示的预付费用中包含强制性预订费和数字费用。 CMA 表示，每节课的费用可能超过 7 英镑。今年早些时候，CMA 勒令另外两家驾校向超过 80,000 名顾客退款，因为他们在网上预订过程中没有提前透露课程总价。CMA 消费者保护执行董事艾玛·科克伦 (Emma Cochrane) 表示：“顾客看到的第一个价格应该是他们支付的价格。”在许多家庭都在关注自己花的每一英镑的时候，重要的是，人们在预订火车票、长途汽车票、假期或驾驶课程时对额外费用并不感到惊讶。”维珍大西洋假期的一位发言人表示，该公司“非常认真地”对待客户的责任，并补充说：“我们始终希望确保他们在通过我们预订假期时能够做出明智的决定。”强制性费用在整个预订过程的多个阶段都会注明。我们正在仔细审查 CMA 提出的观点，并将全力配合其调查。”Trainline 的一位发言人表示，该公司“致力于为客户提供透明的预订体验， “我们已经与 CMA 进行了几个月的积极接触，并正在采取积极措施，以改善向客户收取某些费用的方式。”我们已联系 RED Driving School 征求意见。自去年以来，CMA 有权裁定企业违反了消费者法律，而无需将企业告上法庭。消费者权利组织 Which? 表示，CMA 应该毫不犹豫地使用这些权力，“尤其是在每家公司都收到警告咨询信之后”。消费者主管 Sue Davies哪个？的权利政策表示：“总理上周发表评论称，不公平的定价行为在我们的经济中没有立足之地，此举向其他企业发出了遵守规则的明确信息。“在家庭预算紧张的时候，消费者必须相信企业不会欺骗他们，监管机构愿意介入保护他们的权利。” “订阅陷阱”提前三个月发布8月10日发布“订阅陷阱”禁令提前三个月发布8月10日

title: 能源费用上涨推动英国通胀率升至四个月来最高水平
content: 图片来源，Getty Images作者：Faarea Masud商业记者发布2026年8月19日，英国夏令时07:08更新于1小时前根据最新数据，能源费用上涨导致英国今年截至7月份的通胀率升至2.9%，为四个月来的最高水平。英国国家统计局(ONS)表示，天然气价格以近四年来最大幅度飙升，导致家庭能源上限提高七月份的账单。美以与伊朗战争爆发后，能源成本飙升，限制了全球石油供应。7月份的读数为3月份以来最高，但部分价格增速放缓。食品通胀率为 1.3%，处于近五年来的最低水平。专家表示，通胀数据不太可能影响英国央行在 9 月份的下一次会议上改变其主要利率。能源监管机构 Ofgem 将天然气和电力成本的价格上限提高 13%，使典型账单每年增加 221 英镑，家庭能源成本在 7 月 1 日上涨。据预测，从 10 月份开始，家庭能源费用预计将上涨 4%。 Cornwall Insight 表示，这将使它们达到 2023 年 7 月以来的最高水平。美伊冲突持续存在不确定性，霍尔木兹海峡已被有效关闭，而霍尔木兹海峡是运输石油、液化天然气和其他大宗商品的船舶的关键贸易通道。独立能源咨询公司 Cornwall Insight 补充说，欧洲持续的热浪加剧了能源价格压力，“发电以满足空调和制冷的天然气需求不断增加”英国国家统计局价格主管迈克·哈迪表示，家具价格今年这个时候的跌幅低于平时，增加了通胀的上行压力。他表示，服装的折扣幅度没有那么大。财政大臣约翰·希利表示，伊朗战争继续影响英国的物价，但坚称英国经济具有弹性。“我们已经削减了电费增值税，并将公共汽车票价上限控制在2英镑，为那些感到压力的人提供喘息的空间，”他说。“还有更多的事情要做。”影子财政大臣梅尔·斯特莱德表示，由于工党的“管理不善”，英国对全球冲击没有做好准备，让普通民众“付出了代价”。 图片说明，彭妮·基维尔说，工薪阶层和领取救济金的人会访问她的食品银行。彭妮·基维尔说，生活成本危机将持续下去。她创立了危机支持中心“第二次机会梅德韦”，该中心每两天经营一个折扣食品储藏室。一周，她现在不仅看到了领取福利的人，还看到了工薪阶层。“对负担得起的食物的需求现在遍及社区的各个部分，”她说。 “能源费用仍然太高，工资和收入跟不上。” 英国零售协会首席经济学家 Harvir Dhillon 表示，随着食品通胀放缓，对消费者来说有一些好消息。他表示，7 月份意大利面、橄榄油和新鲜水果的价格均下跌，“表明杂货商之间的激烈竞争牢牢限制了人们每周的购物”。与此同时，汽车燃油价格涨幅放缓至 15.5%，较截至 6 月的 12 个月内，通胀率仍远高于 2025 年的 21.3%。 即将上涨毕马威 (KPMG) 首席经济学家 Yael Selfin 表示，7 月标志着通胀逐渐上升的开始，不过她表示，周三的数字不足以刺激英国央行利率制定决策的变化。她补充说，能源相关成本预计将在未来几个月推高通胀率，达到约 3.5% 的峰值。通胀仍高于预期央行的 2% 目标——央行称这一水平可以保持物价稳定，并让人们和企业能够为未来做好规划。凯投宏观 (Capital Economics) 首席经济学家露丝·格雷戈里 (Ruth Gregory) 预计，只要能源价格不再大幅上涨，通胀率将在“明年年底前”降至目标。“英国央行今年将把利率维持在 3.75%，明年将降至 3%。”英格兰和威尔士特许会计师协会。他说：“通胀上升可能成为未来几个月英国经济增长的最大威胁，因为必需品成本增加，会侵蚀家庭预算。”他补充说，与干旱相关的食品价格上涨也可能即将出现。相关主题通货膨胀经济学英国经济更多关于这个故事英国价格发生了什么？1小时前发表英国经济增长，但专家警告未来几个月面临挑战发表6天前伯纳姆有伟大的想法 - 但它们要花多少钱？7 月 20 日发布

title: 前国防部长呼吁选举，泽连斯基的战时统治面临挑战
content:
乌克兰前国防部长米哈伊洛·费多罗夫呼吁进行战时选举，许多人认为这是自俄罗斯近四年半前发动全面入侵以来对总统弗拉基米尔·泽伦斯基最直接的政治挑战。

上个月作为政府改组的一部分，费多罗夫出人意料地被解雇，他周二表示，“民主无法举行”路透社翻译称，“我们必须找到一种合法、安全和现实的机制，让乌克兰即使在长期战争的情况下也能恢复其全面的民主进程。”费多罗夫说。

他的评论是在 YouTube 上发布的一段长达九分钟多的视频中发表的，其中没有提到泽连斯基的名字。乌克兰法律目前禁止在战时举行选举。

费多罗夫是泽连斯基的前盟友，在乌克兰被广泛视为受欢迎的人物。他在任职大约六个月后于 7 月下旬被解雇，引发了全国主要城市的抗议。

这位 35 岁的人是该国无人机战的倡导者，被誉为为国防部注入活力并带头开展反腐败运动。

费多罗夫发表声明的几个小时前，泽连斯基确认他周三要求议会确认叶夫亨·赫马拉 (Yevhen Khmara) 为乌克兰新任国防部长，从而有效地结束了乌克兰国防部长的任期。费多罗夫复出的大门。

费多罗夫表示乌克兰面临“系统性治理危机”，并谴责官员腐败损害了该国的战争努力，但没有提供任何立法者的姓名。

泽连斯基尚未对费多罗夫的视频声明做出回应。 CNBC 已联系乌克兰外交部征求意见，正在等待答复。

title: 高盛研究了人工智能在哪些方面挤压了劳动力市场。这是它发现的
content:
据高盛称，人工智能正开始对主要发达经济体的劳动力市场构成压力，其影响因行业和资历水平而异。

华尔街投行在研究中发现，自 2022 年下半年以来，人工智能自动化程度较高的行业职位空缺增长普遍放缓，这种关系在德国、澳大利亚和美国尤其明显。

高盛在周三发布的报告中表示，信息和通信服务是受人工智能影响最大的行业之一，自 2022 年以来，几乎所有主要发达经济体的就业增长速度都在放缓。

然而，这些行业的就业仍接近或高于美国以外的长期趋势。

通过更仔细地观察高度受人工智能影响的行业，高盛发现其他发达市场也存在类似的就业逆风模式，尽管总体上更为温和。

呼叫中心、软件出版、管理咨询和高盛表示，发达市场的广告投放已大幅低于历史趋势。

呼叫中心尤其突出。报告显示，目前该行业的就业率低于趋势水平，美国下降了 39%，加拿大下降了 33%，德国下降了 27%。高盛表示，这一模式表明，在拥有能够实现工作自动化的工具的行业中，与人工智能相关的就业压力已经显而易见。

对于那些希望开始职业生涯的人来说，这种影响似乎更为明显。

高盛分析了 800 多种职业的就业增长情况，发现与人工智能相关的阻力在初级工人中最为强烈。它还发现，在被认为被人工智能取代的风险较高的职业中，还发现了额外的负面影响，尽管较小。

在更广泛的劳动力市场中，10%的职业接触人工智能只会对法国、加拿大和美国的年度员工人数增长造成0.1个百分点的拖累。但对于初级工人来说，影响范围在超过0.6个百分点（澳大利亚）到超过0.2个百分点之间（美国）。

总体而言，投资银行得出的结论是，与人工智能相关的招聘压力在全球就业数据中清晰可见，但仍然仅限于相对狭窄的行业和工人。

随着人工智能在发达经济体中的普及，劳动力市场受到影响。

高盛综合了 11 项衡量各国人工智能采用情况的调查，发现主要发达市场的采用率约为 15% 至 20%。

法国、美国、荷兰和英国在人工智能采用方面处于领先地位，而意大利、日本和新西兰则属于采用率较低的发达经济体。

与此同时，主要新兴市场的采用率预计在 10% 至 15% 之间。

title: 特朗普暂停对加拿大征收新关税，并表示各国已接近达成协议
content: 图片来源，Getty Images作者纳丁·尤瑟夫和杰西卡·墨菲29分钟前发布美国总统唐纳德·特朗普表示，随着两国达成贸易协议，他将推迟三天对多种加拿大商品征收新关税。文件，达成协议！”特朗普在社交媒体帖子中表示。这一消息发布不到两小时，距离加拿大近 200 亿美元（280 亿加元）进口商品征收 50% 关税即将生效。双方在多个问题上陷入僵局，包括美国对汽车征收关税以及加拿大许多省份禁止美国酒类销售。特朗普和总理马克·卡尼本周两次通话，在特朗普威胁要设定最后期限后，贸易谈判代表自 7 月以来一直在进行激烈的谈判。 8 月 19 日。 特朗普在帖子中还表示，最终贸易协议可能会让 Keystone XL 管道得以复兴。连接阿尔伯塔省和美国的石油管道被奥巴马和拜登政府封锁。环保主义者和土著团体长期以来一直反对该管道，但特朗普多次表示他希望恢复该项目，该项目每天输送83万桶石油。“伟大的Keystone XL管道，很久以前被瞌睡乔·拜登杀死的，可能会从坟墓中醒来！”特朗普在Truth Social上写道。延期对加拿大谈判代表和边境两侧的企业来说是个好消息，他们警告说新的关税将对两国都有害。自去年1月特朗普重新上任以来，这两个主要贸易伙伴之间的紧张关系不断加剧，并推出了广泛的全球关税计划，颠覆了加拿大和美国之间数十年的自由贸易。特朗普威胁的最新关税将适用于一系列加拿大进口产品，包括葡萄酒、乳制品、水泥、服装和食品。这些是在美国已经对加拿大钢铁和铝、汽车和木材征收的现有关税之外的。加拿大一直在寻求一项协议，让美国放弃或减少对这些关键行业的关税。与此同时，美国一直要求加拿大做出一些让步，包括取消对美国汽车剩余的报复性关税，并调整其乳制品配额，以允许美国奶酪生产商获得更多准入。加拿大还要求禁止美国酒精销售，路透社援引匿名消息人士的报道称，在周三截止日期前的最后几个小时，谈判代表们正在讨论一项将美国对加拿大汽车的关税从 25% 降至 15% 的协议。但两国未能就哪些车辆有资格获得关税减免达成一致，美国推动该政策仅适用于含有大量美国制造成分的汽车。卡尼还需要省长们支持恢复美国酒类销售，因为酒类销售是由各省而不是联邦政府控制的。受美国汽车关税打击最严重的安大略省省长道格·福特表示，只有在达成“公平协议”的情况下，他才愿意解除酒类禁令。周二，美国商会推动达成协议，在一份声明中表示，“更高的关税将损害两国经济，增加美国家庭的成本，进一步扰乱关键的供应链，依赖美国-墨西哥-加拿大贸易协定下的贸易的1300万个美国就业岗位面临风险”。相关话题加拿大美国特朗普关税唐纳德·特朗普

title: 中国机器人巨头优树上市首日飙升
content: Image source,VCG via Getty ImagesImage caption,Unitree's humanoid robots have been at the centre of a huge marketing pushByOsmond ChiaBusiness reporterPublished19 August 2026, 02:49 BSTUpdated 1 hour agoThe world's biggest humanoid robot maker Unitree Robotics made its stock market debut in Shanghai on Wednesday, with its shares soaring by more than 600%.In the highly anticipated initial public offering (IPO),the Chinese firm's shares opened at 1,100 yuan (Â£120.60; $163.12), well above the 150.8 yuan offer price.The listing on the tech-focused Star Market - which is widely known as China's Nasdaq - marks a milestone for Beijing's ambitious plans for the country's robotics industry.It comes as the US and China are locked in a battle to dominate the global market for robots and artificial intelligence (AI) models that power them.Unitree's debut marks the first humanoid robot maker to be listed in mainland China.Robots like automated industrial equipment and smart vacuum cleaners are already widely used in factories, warehouses and homes.Now, the humanoid robotics industry is attracting huge amounts of investment as major companies - including Tesla, BYD and Amazon - are developing two-legged machines capable of performing tasks usually carried out by people.What is Unitree?Unitree, officially known as Yushu Technology Co Ltd, was founded in 2016.It has become a robotics industry leader, selling a wide range of devices from sensors and automated arms to four-legged and human-like machines.The firm shipped more than 5,500 humanoid robots last year as demand for the technology grows.Unitree is one of the few companies in the sector to make money, delivering a net profit of 278 million yuan in 2025.It is a fierce rival to developers in the US as it produces robots with similar features but at lower prices.The company - which plays a key role in Beijing's ambitions to be a global leader in cutting-edge technologies - is based in Hangzhou, in eastern China.The region is home to a so-called golden cluster zone of robotics firms, which have been boosted by huge government investments.That support helped drive a more than threefold increase in the number of Chinese robotics firms between 2020 and 2024, according to state-run China Daily.Robots are also seen as a potential solution to issues posed by China's ageing population, which is expected to lead to a shortage of workers in the country, according to Fei Qin, an associate professor at the University of Bath.Beijing considers the robotics sector a "strategic priority" in its pursuit of leadership in advanced technology, she said."Robots are where AI leaves the screen and enters the economy" in factories, hospitals and, potentially, the home, Qin added.Image source,Future Publishing via Getty ImagesImage caption,Elon Musk's Tesla is developing a humanoid robot called OptimusUS robots tend to have more user-friendly software but it is difficult to ignore the lower prices offered by Chinese manufacturers, said Harold Soh, a researcher from the National University of Singapore.Unitree's robot dogs start at $2,700, a fraction of the roughly $70,000 price tag for Boston Dynamics' four-legged device, Spot."They're not exactly comparable because some of Unitree's dogs are much smaller," Soh said. "But the price is a big difference."Unitree has been selling humanoid robots since 2023, with its $13,500 child-sized G1 model hitting the market the following year.Meanwhile, major US rivals - including Elon Musk's Tesla - have yet to start delivering rival products.Image source,CCTVImage caption,Unitree's humanoids performed at a Lunar New Year showcase ths yearThe G1, along with other Unitree robots have been at the centre of a huge marketing push ahead of the firm's IPO.This week, its machines are competing in the 2026 World Humanoid Robot Games in Beijing. The event features hundreds of teams competing in events such as running and football as well as less sporty challenges like box opening and sorting library books.Earlier this year, Unitree's robots caught the eye of the public and researchers when its G1 robots put on a display of martial arts moves during China's Spring Festival Gala.The event, broadcast on state TV in February, showed the robots performing a "full range of motions, live on stage, in a way we'd never seen before," said robotics researcher David Hsu."It was an indication of a rise of an industry," Hsu added.A bellwether for robotics firms?Unitree's market debut is seen by some experts as a gauge of investor appetite for the fast-growing humanoid robotics sector.The listing has given the public a rare chance to invest in a humanoid robotics company and could set a benchmark for other manufacturers, said Jack Pearson from investment firm RoboStrategy.The listing also marks a "turning point" for China's robotics industry, as Unitree's success comes even as the US is curbing imports of foreign-made robots, Pearson said.Unitree's IPO comes almost three years after smaller Chinese rival UBTech Robotics listed on the Hong Kong stock market.In July this year, UBTech drew global attention when it unveiled what Chinese state media described as a "life-sized, hyper-realistic humanoid robot designed as a companion that offers users emotional support and everyday interaction."More robot makers, including Leju Robotics and AgiBot, are expected to follow UBTech and Unitree with stock market listings in the coming months.Image source,AFP via Getty ImagesImage caption,UBTech showcased its line of life-like humanoid robots this yearBut the optimism around the industry comes as some experts have voiced doubts over demand for robots for uses outside industrial and commercial settings.Robots are still years away from working effectively in homes, Soh said.Developers need to address issues like longer battery life, privacy safeguards and reliabilty, he said.Initially, the market will be for robots being used in places like factories and hospitals, he added.China-US tech rivalryRobots and AI have become the latest flashpoint in the rivalry between the US and China, as both nations view them as strategically important industries.US President Donald Trump's administration said in July that it wouldban new Chinese-made humanoid and quadruped robotsover national security concerns and protecting US manufacturing.Beijing rejected the claim, accusing Washington of "politicising" trade issues.The White House has also set tough restrictions on other Chinese technology - including AI models, electric cars, semiconductors and drones.China's dominance of the robotics industry highlights a broader issue faced by Washington as Chinese firms become more "deeply embedded" in global manufacturing, said Christine Wan from the Peterson Institute for International Economics."Other countries may be reluctant to sharply reduce their reliance on Chinese suppliers if doing so would significantly disrupt domestic manufacturing," Wan said.Why human-shaped robots loom large in Musk's Tesla plansPublished7 November 2025Who will win the race to develop a humanoid robot?Published25 April 2025The Chinese robot army transforming the UK's retail industryPublished29 JulySo far, Western robots have not made the same impact on factory floors or in the consumer market.Boston Dynamics, a major US robotics developer, has said it willroll out human-like machines in car maker Hyundai's factoriesin two years' time. The South Korean firm bought a majority stake in Boston Dynamics in 2021.Other US firms, like Amazon and Tesla, have also announced plans to use humanoid robots in their operations.Earlier this year, Musk's firm announced that it would use its manufacturing plant in California that made Model S and X cars toproduce its line of Optimus humanoid robots.Amazon, which tested theuse of humanoid robots in its warehousesin 2023, told the BBC it has completed a pilot scheme for the technology and is continuing its research into next-generation robotics.The BBC has also contacted Tesla and Boston Dynamics for comment on their humanoid robot plans.One thing is clear, said Hsu, the US has lost the lead on robotics that it had a decade ago."We no longer hear about American robotics companies in the news. It's the Chinese robot companies that are making news today," he added."They have replaced America as the cool kids on the block."Listen to the BBC News World Service Asia Specific podcast:China's humanoid robot boomRelated topicsInternational BusinessRoboticsChinaEconomicsArtificial intelligenceStock markets

title: 中国后空翻机器人制造商Unitree在上海上市首日股价上涨542%
content:
周三早盘交易中，这家中国人形机器人制造商在上海上市，其股价上涨了 542%。

这家总部位于杭州的机器人制造商的后空翻和跳舞机引起了全球关注，根据其招股说明书，该公司在 IPO 中筹集了约 61 亿元人民币（9.05 亿美元）。股价在早些时候触及 1,100 元人民币后，升至每股 968.1 元人民币。

根据公司备案文件，此次 IPO 还获得了中国人工智能公司 DeepSeek 的支持，该公司投资了约 1.408 亿元人民币。 Unitree的现有投资者还包括中国科技巨头腾讯。

Unitree的产品阵容涵盖可以行走和用灵巧的双手操纵物体的双足人形机器人，以及用于危险检测等任务的四足机器人。

在上市之前，Unitree周一推出了一款名为“超人”的新型人形机器人，据称它可以从站立位置跳跃两米，奔跑速度高达12.66米

宇树科技是继上个月存储芯片制造商长鑫存储上市后，最新登陆上海科创板的中国科技巨头，其股价在首日交易中飙升 466%。

摩根士丹利 6 月份将中国仿人机器人出货量预测上调至 50,000 台，几乎是之前预测 28,000 台的两倍。该银行估计，中国的类人机器人市场将从今年的 20 亿美元增长到 2030 年的 150 亿美元。

该银行进一步预计，中国的试点项目将在今年下半年开始进行更广泛的部署，预计全尺寸类人机器人将占出货量的 30% 左右，到 2028 年将升至 70%。

title: 加州 AG Bonta 表示，针对 Meta 的案件涉及“恢复和扭曲”，而不是损害赔偿
content:
在针对 Meta 的高风险儿童安全案件的第一天辩论之后，加州总检察长 Rob Bonta 周二表示，审判的重点是“民事处罚、赔偿和扭曲”，而不是主要涉及金钱。

“这不是损害赔偿案，”Bonta 在当天庭审结束后的新闻发布会上表示。

预计将在奥克兰联邦法院进行审判持续六到七周。 Bonta 和来自科罗拉多州、新泽西州和肯塔基州的总检察长共同领导了对 Meta 的审判，并代表由 29 名 AG 组成的两党团体，指控 Facebook 和 Instagram 的设计和功能鼓励儿童上瘾行为，并损害他们的心理健康。

Meta 的律师此前曾警告称，合并案件可能导致罚款高达 1.4 万亿美元，或大致相当于该公司的市值。州总检察长上周告诉联邦法官伊冯·冈萨雷斯·罗杰斯 (Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers)，2000 亿美元的可能性更大。

咨询陪审团已就职审理此案，但冈萨雷斯·罗杰斯最终将决定 Meta 的命运。这与今年早些时候埃隆·马斯克和萨姆·阿尔特曼之间的审判所采用的设置相同。

代表各州的律师指控 Meta 违反了联邦和州法律，例如《儿童在线隐私保护法》(COPPA) 以及各种消费者保护法规。 Bonta 表示，各州律师“向法院提交了文件”，其中包括与 Facebook 和 Instagram 等应用程序的年轻用户数量相关的某些统计数据，作为确定潜在民事处罚的标准。

“需要明确的是，我们不会要求 1.4 万亿美元，”Bonta 周二表示。他表示，这是“根据该数据计算出的最高可能数字”，并且“这是 Meta 估计的数字”。 Meta 对这一说法提出异议。邦塔表示，原告“将要求以现有民事处罚总额的形式获得重大经济收益，作为本案的重要且适当的部分。”他说，“法官将酌情决定具体内容。”

该审判源于 2023 年提起的诉讼。在开庭辩论中，加州副总检察长梅根·奥尼尔 (Megan O'Neill) 提出了针对 Meta 的指控。与其他相关的社交媒体审判类似，包括 Meta 和谷歌旗下 YouTube 在 3 月份败诉的洛杉矶人身伤害诉讼，奥尼尔的论点集中在指控上，即 Meta 首席执行官马克·扎克伯格等高管的公开声明与该公司对儿童心理健康的内部研究相矛盾，并歪曲了伤害的真实程度。

“Meta 是世界上最大、最强大的公司之一，开展了一场欺骗、误导用户的活动，奥尼尔告诉咨询陪审团。

代表 Meta 的 Covington & Burling 审判律师保罗·施密特 (Paul Schmidt) 对奥尼尔的论点提出了质疑，并对 Meta 高管在有关儿童安全的声明中误导公众的观点提出了异议。

“当您听到我们将向您询问的证据时，这是否证明了他们所声称的具体内容？” 施密特对八名陪审团成员说道。

对于涉嫌的违规行为，州律师希望 Meta 删除 13 岁以下儿童的所有个人数据以及使用这些信息训练的相关算法和模型，并删除某些设计元素，例如无限滚动、自动播放和美容功能。

此次审判是在新墨西哥州 AG Raúl Torrez 最近在法庭上胜诉 Meta 后进行的，该诉讼导致这家社交媒体巨头被指示向一项减排基金支付 5.67 亿美元，作为其中一部分涉及儿童性剥削指控的案件第二阶段。陪审团已于 3 月份裁定，Meta 应因违反新墨西哥州不公平行为法而被迫支付 3.75 亿美元的民事罚款。

Bonta 指出，Meta 并不是唯一一家受到各州总检察长瞄准的社交媒体公司。他说，几个州“现在已经有针对 TikTok 的未决诉讼”，他“也担心 YouTube 和 Snap”。他说，Meta 只是“排在第一位”，在全州范围内寻求“一些全行业解决方案”。

“谁先走？谁最后走？理想情况下，他们都同时走，”邦塔说。 “这是不可能的。在理想的世界中，他们都将致力于对所有孩子进行相同的改革和改变，并确保他们的安全。”

title: 中国白酒制造商茅台的低迷对中国经济有何影响
content:
BEIJING — Walk down most streets in China and you'll find a liquor store advertising premium spirits brand Moutai, along with posters of resale prices by vintage year.

It's a testament to how intertwined the red-and-white-labeled bottles have been with China's economy in recent decades. The 53% alcohol content "baijiu" was long a staple at government and business dinners for toasts and sealing deals, so much so that Moutai's stock became a market bellwether.

But the spirits company is now struggling, as China's business world adapts to the tech-heavy artificial intelligence era.

Kweichow Moutai'shalf-year report this month showed a rare drop in net profit, down by 1.95% to 44.5 billion yuan ($6.6 billion). It was the first decline for the first six months of a year since 2014, and only the second such drop based on data going back to 2002, according to Wind Information data.

The latest results followed a decline of 4.5% in net profit for all of 2025 — the first annual decline on record, data showed.

It's all related to changes in the economic environment, said Ye Yuhua, fund manager at Ba Luo Fund. That's according to a CNBC translation of Mandarin.

China's economy in the second quarter expanded at itsweakest pacesince the fourth quarter of 2022, with urban fixed-asset investment, including real estate development and infrastructure projects, declining 5.7% in the first six months from a year earlier.

When the real estate sector thrived, there were naturally more scenarios involving premium baijiu consumption, Ye said. Now with the economic shift to high-end tech, he noted the people involved with this emerging industry aren't as inclined to drink baijiu.

"It's an irreversible trend," he said. "Baijiu has become a saturated market."

China's anti-corruption crackdown has intensified in recent years, contributing to drag on retail sales. In 2020, Chinese authorities also tightened restrictions on real estate developers' ability to borrow heavily for growth, clamping down on a construction-heavy sector that had come to determine a quarter of the economy.

Moutai was the largest listed company in mainland China by market capitalization from 2020 to 2023, according to Wind Information data.

Shares briefly fell Monday after the weekend release of its semi-annual financial report, driving its year-to-date losses to 5.7% as of Tuesday. The stock is has declined on an annual basis for four consecutive years.

The half-year report also showed China's state funds Central Huijin and China Securities Finance, sometimes dubbed part of the "National Team," were no longer among the 10 largest holders of Moutai stock.

Institutional investor sentiment likely troughed given the exit of Huijin and China Securities Finance from its top 10 shareholders in the second quarter, Citi sad in a report.

The most significant signal from the baijiu company's latest financial report is that the value of Moutai in business negotiations is shrinking, said Dongfang Li, an independent stock analyst.

However, he pointed out that Moutai's high 90% gross margin, its profitability and stable dividend continue to attract institutional funds. Li expects institutional allocation to persist.

Citi analysts attributed the decline to the company's transition from wholesale to direct-to-consumer sales rather than soft demand. The bank maintained its "buy" rating on Moutai.

They expect Moutai to benefit from a recent rotation back into China's consumer sector, with global long-only investors cautiously returning to high-quality, large-cap consumer staples.

Morningstar similarly said in a report that a mix shift toward direct-to-consumer sales likely distorted Moutai's payment line, while underlying demand appeared stronger than reported revenue growth. More broadly, it said Moutai is its preferred pick within China's baijiu sector, citing its competitive position and deepening market-oriented reform.

Looking ahead, both Citi and Morningstar mentioned the upcoming Mid-Autumn Festival in their reports. Citi said Moutai may have been incentivized to shift some inventory supply from the second quarter to the third, when the Mid-Autumn Festival falls, to capture the full benefit of its second round of price hikes, which took effect on July 18.

Morningstar, meanwhile, said recent price hikes and seasonally stronger Mid-Autumn Festival sales should support a gradual earnings pickup from the second half. It expects Moutai's net profit to grow at an 8% compound annual growth rate from 2025 to 2030.

Moutai has implemented two rounds of price hikes for its flagship liquor this year.

Investors, meanwhile, are still waiting for the baijiu market to recover before making strategic moves, said Wenjie Ding, investment strategist for global capital investment at China Asset Management.

She noted ETF data showed net outflows for the better part of this year from food and beverage companies with significant baijiu weighting, although sentiment could have improved modestly this month.

As Beijing hasleft real estate behindin pursuit oftechnological development, will Moutai be replaced by another stock as well, signaling a changing of the old guard for good?

Li pointed out that since the beginning of the year, several Chinese tech names have surpassed Moutai in market value at different points. He noted memory chip company CXMT that listed last month has a market capitalization about 2.5-times that of Moutai.

"The market is shifting from the traditional economy's logic of steady growth to high growth potential and global competitiveness brought about by technological innovation," he said in Chinese, according to a CNBC translation.

title: 到处都是核武器？破损的美国核保护伞正在推动盟友权衡防御选择，增加核扩散的风险
content:
For decades, allies worldwide rested in the comfort of the U.S. nuclear umbrella, confident they didn't need their own weapons of mass destruction.

That belief is rapidly evaporating as President Donald Trump'slatest National Defense Strategy for2026 dropped any explicit mention of extended deterrence and has pressed allies to spend more of their own money on defenses.

The change is prompting more governments to reconsider whether to acquire nuclear weapons of their own, raising the risk of a proliferation cascade, analysts say.

Allies almost universally perceive Washington as becoming more "disengaged and unreliable," prompting "various flavors of strategic autonomy," said Ankit Panda, senior fellow in the Nuclear Policy Program of the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace.

Most recently,U.S. President Donald Trumpordered a reduction in joint military exercises with ally South Korea, saying that the exercises sent a signal that was "totally inappropriate and hostile" to North Korea.

Earlier last month, the U.S.opened talkson peaceful South Korean enrichment and reprocessing, and signed a Saudi civil-nuclear pact thatreportedly couldcreate a path to domestic enrichment.

In a bid to strengthen Europe's independence, French President Emmanuel Macron announced in March thecountry's first warhead increasesince 1992 and promised to extend its nuclear umbrella to other countries in the bloc under the so-called"forward deterrence" partnership. Nine countries, including Germany and Greece, have joined the initiative.

Japan is also doing more in thenuclear defense realmunder Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, whose reluctance to rule out revising Japan's three non-nuclear principles late last year has drawn scrutiny,fueling speculation that she could shift awayfrom the decades-old commitment to refrain from assuming any role in deployment of nuclear weapons.

Leaders of Lithuania and Finland, both sharing a border with Russia, have moved closer toscrapping the longstanding ban on domestic deploymentof nuclear weapons.

None of these developments amounts to a decision to build a bomb — but one state's efforts to increase its security can leave adversaries feeling less secure, potentially encouraging them to strike first, said Shounak Set, a research fellow at the S. Rajaratnam School of International Studies in Singapore.

"You cannot build or deploy a nuclear deterrent without immediately raising tensions and forcing adversaries to react," said Andrew Facini, senior fellow at the Council on Strategic Risks, possibly accelerating the security risks a proliferator is trying to avoid.

Defense ministries in the U.S. and Japan, as well as the European External Action Service, the bloc's diplomatic service office, did not respond to CNBC's requests for comments.

The best example now is Iran, whose pursuit of enriched uranium was at least partially responsible for the current war in the Middle East. The Trump administration has repeatedly said that "Iran cannot be allowed to have a nuclear weapon," and the joint U.S.-Israeli strikes in 2025 were aimed at that objective.

While Iran is not known to have a nuclear weapon, now, with the war, "we don't know if by the act of attacking them we have pushed the Iranians, fully and finally, to decide to actually go nuclear, which is a decision they had not made as of yet," said Alexandra Bell, president and CEO of the Bulletin of Atomic Scientists.

All nine nuclear-armed states — the U.S., Russia, China, the U.K., France, India, Pakistan, North Korea and Israel — have continued to modernize and expand their arsenals, fueling an arms race that researchers say has"new risk" of miscalculationamid escalating tensions.

Russia and the U.S. together remain the overwhelming nuclear powers, together possessing around 83% of useable nuclear warheads, according to a June report by the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute. "By reaching for nuclear solutions, states are creating new risks and fueling arms-race dynamics," Hans Kristensen, a senior fellow at the firm, said in the report.

He added that countries' accelerated push for nuclear weapons will likely reverse decades of demobilization efforts in the coming years.

"The evidence is growing that the nuclear weapon states are sidelining, and even walking away from, their disarmament commitments and are instead flexing their nuclear muscles," said Kristensen.

Out of the over 12,000 nuclear warheads owned by nuclear powers, more than 9,000 are held in military stockpiles for potential use. An estimated 4,012 warheads were deployed with missiles and aircraft, while up to 2,200 were kept on high alert, meaning they could be launched within minutes.

ACarnegie report in September last yearput it bluntly, saying that "if more actors acquire them — whether friendly or unfriendly nations or subnational groups — the world will be a more dangerous place, for the United States and for everyone else."

"A proliferation cascade is a compounding risk," said Facini, as every new nuclear state multiplies the chances for miscalculation, shrinks decision-making windows, and potentially sparks "regional arms-races where even conventional clashes can carry existential stakes."

Introducing nuclear weapons into volatile regional disputes also drastically raises the stakes for unintended escalation, Facini added.

A new round of review held at United Nations headquarters in Mayfailed to reach a consensus,with UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres warning that theNuclear Non-Proliferation Treatyis "eroding."

The treaty, entered into force in 1970 and extended indefinitely in 1995, has as its central bargain that non-nuclear states agree never to acquire nuclear weapons, while nuclear states share the benefits of peaceful nuclear technology and pursue nuclear disarmament.

The treaty has "by and large stemmed the flow of mass proliferation," said Bell. Without those safeguards, more nuclear material, facilities and expertise would be in circulation, raising the risk of nuclear terrorism, albeit from a low base, she said.

Bell urged Washington to reduce the incentives for other states to acquire nuclear weapons. "Building things is hard. Breaking things is very easy," she said. "If we break the NPT, we may never recover from that lapse in security."

title: 关键技术通过转入地下保持安全
content: Image source,EarthgridImage caption,"Like lighting a rocket" the Earthgrid machine operates at very high temperaturesByChris BaraniukTechnology ReporterPublished16 minutes agoA wall of white granite towered above a small team of engineers gathered in a California quarry. The ancient, ultra-hard material before them was, to most things, completely impermeable.Then the rock-melting tunnel-boring machine (TBR) roared to life."It's kind of like igniting a rocket," says Troy Helming, founder and chief executive of EarthGrid, as he describes the initially loud process of lighting up three plasma torches at the front of his company's machine.Those torches, set within a spinning head, soon quieten down as they produce a stream of super-heated plasma reaching 27,000C - significantly hotter than the surface of the Sun.During the California test this January, EarthGrid's cigar-shaped boring machine chewed through three metres of granite. "We create, basically, a tornado â a violent vortex inside the tunnel," says Helming, as he explains how this helps the machine to suck away debris, which at times takes the form of lava."I actually got a little bit emotional watching it," adds the entrepreneur. "I've been waiting for this moment for 10 years."Emerging technologies like this could make tunnel boring quicker and easier. Putting electricity or telecommunications cables, substations, data centres and other critical infrastructure underground, while good for securing such equipment, has long been a very expensive and difficult option.Engineering firms told BBC News they are seeing rising demand for undergrounding, in part due to Russia's war with Ukraine, which has revealedjust how vulnerableabove-ground facilities can be to drone attacks.Helming says he has fielded interest from companies that want to use his tunnel boring machine for power and fibre optic cables, or pipelines that could transport water, natural gas, or ammonia, for example.One project the company has eyed up would involve boring tunnels for an underground freight-distribution system around airports and warehouses. "To take more trucks off the road," says Helming.The January TBR test went well, though the machine "over-bored" slightly to the top and left of the tunnel, says Helming. His team plans to adjust the machine so that it will create a vortex that spins in alternate directions every five minutes or so, in order to correct this, and they hope the TBR could see commercial deployment as early as next year.Image source,EarthgridImage caption,The Earthgrid machine can blast its way through solid rockHumanshave long buried thingsin the ground to protect them. Doing it safely and cost-effectively with modern infrastructure is hard but sometimes, even in remotest places, it's an option worth taking."What we're seeing is that brutal materiality is still important," says Alexander RE Taylor, senior lecturer in communications at the University of Exeter. He has identifiedwhat he calls a "data bunker boom",externalin which data centres are increasingly going underground.One data centre completed earlier this year was installedin a corner of the Dolomite Mountains,externalin Italy.Freshly excavated caverns 100m underground sit next to stores that have been used for sparkling wine, apples and cheese in recent years.Trentino DataMine's naturally cool space makes it cheaper and less energy-intensive to keep servers cool.Chief executive Dennis Bonn adds: "Ninety million cubic metres of dolomite rock provide natural protection against physical intrusion, electromagnetic interference, seismic events and hydrogeological risks - levels of protection that simply cannot be replicated above ground."Image source,Trentino DataMineImage caption,Trentino DataMine says its facility provides "security designed by nature"Elsewhere, some tech is burrowing into the seabed. Subsea internet cables, which may run for thousands of kilometres beneath oceans, areoccasionally damaged by ship anchors.There isevidence to suggest,externalthat, as burying part or all of the cables has become more common, faults with these cables have become rarer, per kilometre of deployed cable, explains Lane Burdette, senior analyst at TeleGeography, a telecoms market research firm."Submarine cables are increasingly being buried up to three meters deep," she says. "In some fault-prone areas, they are buried along their entire lengths."Taylor says various examples demonstrate that keeping things underground, or deep inside caves, is an effective defensive strategy."The tunnels thatAl-Qaeda were usingwere a major strategic problem for the US [during the war in Afghanistan]," he adds. More recently, Iran's notoriously difficult-to-bustunderground nuclear facilitieshave gained much attention.The war in Ukraine, and other geopolitical events, have "definitely had an impact" on demand for undergrounding in some areas, says Robbie McGoran, head of work winning and business development at Joseph Gallagher, a civil engineering and tunnelling firm.Countries bordering Russia are increasingly asking about undergrounding. "They're very cautious about who they'll even let do their work â and also burying [infrastructure] and making sure it's well protected. We are noticing that," he adds.McGoran also says that technologies such as laser-guidance systems and gyroscopes, which help machines work out their position relative to the world around them, have made tunnelling more accurate in recent years.However, there are still significant challenges, from releasing potentially dangerous gases locked in the ground to occasional flooding issues. Dramatic innovation in tunnel boring equipment, significantly increasing the rate at which tunnels can be carved out, does not come along very often."We usually measure [progress] in millimetres per minute," says McGoran.Image source,National GridImage caption,The London Power Tunnels project involved 18 miles of tunnels under LondonIn the UK, there isn't a noticeable shift towards putting critical infrastructure underground yet, says Mark Neller, energy leader for Europe, India, Middle East and Africa at engineering consultants Arup.Though in some places, tunnels are clearly necessary. Neller and colleagues worked on the Â£1bnLondon Power Tunnels project, which involved building 18 miles (29km) of tunnels under London to house large electricity cables.This was the perfect choice for such a busy urban area but because tunnelling can be several times more expensive than above-ground cable infrastructure, Neller says that, elsewhere, simply installing additional circuits can provide sufficient resilience."That's actually a much more cost-effective way," he says. "The electricity system [in Great Britain] is designed with quite a lot of redundancy built into it."Richard Little, infrastructure policy consultant and editor of the Journal of Critical Infrastructure Policy, remembers the latter days of the Cold War, when it was the threat of all-out nuclear war that made bunker-building a frequent talking point in the West.To this day, Switzerland mandates that every citizen must haveaccess to a nuclear bunker,external. Many apartment buildings in the country have such facilities in their basements."A lot of it was real Dr Strangelove stuff," says Little, referring to discussions around bunker-building during President Ronald Reagan's administration. "The world's going to end but I guess we'll maybe harbour a few hundred critical people down here and they'll survive."Little, who authored policy documents regardingunderground critical infrastructure,externalduring the 1990s, adds, "It became obvious rather quickly that you can't put everything underground."Today, it might be worth identifying specific facilities that would be difficult to restart or replace, were they attacked, as candidates for undergrounding. "The first thing that occurred to me was [computer] chip manufacturing," says Little, offering an example."Underground facilities, I'm sure in certain instances, would make a great deal of sense â but it's all about what's critical."Related topicsInternational BusinessTechnology of BusinessMore Technology of BusinessAI is 'not smart' so what's next in artificial intelligence?Published3 JulyIndia's 'blue gold' starts a new drinks industryPublished12 JuneThe abundant but expensive energy source that's under your feetPublished26 June

title: “因一双价值 2 英镑的凉鞋而被禁止”：为什么一些卖家抱怨 Vinted
content: Image caption,Emma Neil was banned from Vinted after listing a pair of sandals which it deemed to be fakePublished26 minutes agoSingle mum Emma Neil was a huge fan of Vinted, using it most days to sell old things and buy clothes for her children.That was until she bought a pair of sandals for Â£3, found they didn't fit so relisted them for Â£2 then was permanently banned. Vinted said there had been "fraudulent activity, such as selling counterfeit items"."I did feel like a criminal," says Neil - one of several thousands complaining of being wrongly suspended or permanently banned, spending days trapped in a system of what they believe are AI generated responses.Vinted's preloved buying and selling community has grown rapidly with 17 million UK users - it says the "overwhelming majority" have a positive experience.However, Neil is one of more than 4,000 Vinted users who have logged their experiences on sadvintedfaces.com, a website set up by freelance marketeer Catherine Warrilow, who became so frustrated with the platform she decided to find out if others were having problems too.Image source,Catherine WarrilowImage caption,Catherine Warrilow has heard from thousands of unhappy Vinted users"It was the number of hours I was spending sending irate messages back to Vinted and getting what felt like automated responses, copy and paste... I was going round in circles, and I was the one losing out," she says.Warrilow logged 2,609 users being banned or suspended, 1,618 with a permanent ban and 2,526 who said they were ignored by Vinted customer service."I think the automation they're using isn't working properly," says Warrilow."It's detecting fraud if you change the price of something. It's detecting a counterfeit item for a second hand pair of Zara jeans."Matthew Connor is one of the biggest professional sellers on Vinted and relies on it for his livelihood with some ten thousand top reviews. He also thinks the system isn't working the way it used to.Image source,Matthew ConnorImage caption,Matthew Connor is a pro seller who says his ban saw him lose thousands in potential sales"I noticed at the start of this year, there were a lot of fake items on there. I think they panicked, rightly so...and they've reacted with AI."But last month, he found himself permanently banned because of "fraudulent activity, such as selling counterfeit items" after listing a used North Face fleece."I wouldn't jeopardise my business by selling a fake. This is my livelihood," he said."Essentially someone's walked into my business and sacked me, removed my business from the internet with no prior warning."Two weeks later, Connor had his ban lifted after he appealed. Vinted said it was a mistake. He's relieved but has also lost thousands of pounds of potential sales.Appeal failedNeil's appeal to have her ban overturned failed."I don't understand how they could say that to me...it's just unbelievable," she said. "They weren't specifically branded. I think they're like a Shoe Zone make.""I'm absolutely devastated because I love Vinted and I used it for so long and for so many different things...but now obviously that's all ended."Vinted said it doesn't comment on individual cases. In a statement it said its teams worked hard every day to maintain a safe and trusted marketplace using a combination of trained moderation teams, member reports and detection tools to identify potential breaches of its catalogue rules."Where members believe a decision has been made in error, they can appeal and each case will be reviewed individually by our Member Support Team," a Vinted spokesperson said.Has Vinted lost the human touch?An online business the size of Vinted with millions of transactions needs automation and communicates electronically with its users. But as it grows, has it lost the human touch?Consumer expert Helen Dewdney, who runs the Complaining Cow website, has recently seen a sharp increase in complaints and requests for advice about Vinted."It does boil down to customer service," she believes."We know that AI makes a lot of mistakes...it's too difficult to get to a human being... we know that people prefer people...you just ask anybody that they're sick of all the bots."Dewdney says anyone who believes they've been unfairly banned or suspended should first go through Vinted's own appeal process. She also suggests contacting Vinted's legal team and making a subject access request, or SAR, which can give users access to information about how a decision affecting their account was made.Vinted stresses that assessments of appeals are always carried out by its human review team.Too big, too fast?The Lithuanian based firm has built a business worth billions on a simple idea which has changed the way millions of us buy and sell second hand clothes. It's now in 26 countries and expanded into new services, like Vinted Pro for professional sellers and more categories including electronics and toys.For Connor, it's a no brainer as there are no fees for sellers. He says although the platform's "done a lot of things right" he believes it got "too big too fast".And he'd be prepared to pay a premium fee or fees on his sales to contribute to having "some sort of a human voice" to talk to.As for Warrilow, she just wants her old Vinted back."I do believe they could fix it," she says.But until they do, she says she's staying off the platform as it wasn't worth the stress.Get in touchShare your experience with Vinted.Contact formRelated topicsCompaniesOnline shopping

title: 吉姆·克莱默 (Jim Cramer) 表示市场过于消极——这正在创造买入机会
content:
CNBC 的吉姆·克莱默 (Jim Cramers) 周二表示，围绕市场的持续负面情绪正在为那些愿意忽略头条新闻并忍受短期波动的投资者创造机会。

他发表此番言论之际，美国国债收益率上升、通胀持续存在以及油价上涨令股市承压。三大股指当天全部收跌。 30年期国债收益率触及5.33%，为近二十年来的最高水平，而由于美伊谈判仍陷入僵局，布伦特原油价格突破每桶90美元。然而，克莱默认为，这些担忧掩盖了经济复苏的迹象。

“我知道‘不错’并不是一个响亮的号角。但如果背景良好，你肯定会得到比你看到的更好的价格，”《疯狂金钱》主持人说。 “也许这就是思考问题的方式。这就是机会，而且成本似乎是可控的，即使这可能不是确切的底部。”

“我是说，情况并不全是坏事……情况可能会变得更好，”他说。

克莱默指出，石油和债券是两个可能过度担忧的领域。虽然原油价格上涨加剧了通胀压力，但他预计，随着供应量增加，布伦特原油价格不会大幅上涨至 100 美元以上。他表示，较高的国债收益率最终也可能吸引买家，因为投资者可以锁定越来越有吸引力的政府债务回报。债券收益率与价格成反比，因此在其他条件相同的情况下，买家的增加会压低收益率。

他还看到了技术领域的机会。克莱默表示，由于纳斯达克 100 指数的空头押注数量创历史新高，他正寻求利用这一弱点逐步买入遭受重创的数据中心股票。他重点介绍了美光科技，CNBC 投资俱乐部运营的克莱默慈善信托基金 (Cramer's Charitable Trust) 最近在人工智能基础设施中使用的内存需求强劲时购买了美光科技。

弹性的消费者支出给了克莱默另一个不必过于悲观的理由。Airbnb 报告了强劲的旅行需求，而俱乐部控股的家得宝 (Home Depot) 则实现了克莱默所说的“五年来最好的季度”。

“我只能告诉你的是，最后如今，我们是一个服务经济体，”克莱默说。 “如果服务表现良好，那么你就不能太消极。”

克莱默并不是说市场的问题已经消失，也不是说市场已经真正触底。他的观点是，即使部分经济仍然强劲，普遍的悲观情绪仍在压低价格——如果投资者的担忧没有完全成为现实，这可能会给投资者提供一个更具吸引力的切入点。

title: 标准普尔 500 指数连续第三个下跌日后，股票期货几乎没有变化：实时更新
content:
美国周二晚间，由于全球债券溃败和油价上涨打压投资者情绪，主要股指连续第三个交易日下跌，股票期货接近持平。

道琼斯工业平均指数期货上涨 3 点，即 0.01%。标准普尔 500 指数期货持平，而纳斯达克 100 指数期货下跌 0.04%。

华尔街正在摆脱亏损。道琼斯指数下跌 116 点，即 0.2%，而标准普尔 500 指数则下跌 0.7%。纳斯达克综合指数下跌 1.3%，是三者中跌幅最大的。

随着美国和其他地区的债券收益率创下新的里程碑，科技股尤其下跌。周二，30 年期国债收益率创下 19 年来新高，而日本 10 年期国债收益率则达到 30 年来的最高水平。德国30年期国债收益率触及2011年以来的最高点，而法国30年期国债利率则达到2008年以来的最高水平。

尽管长期债券收益率达到数十年来的高点，但股市反应却相当平淡。投资者押注，持续的经济增长，加上公司历史上强劲的盈利，将在收益率上升的情况下继续支撑股市。

“我认为，最终，经济足够强劲，”Trivariate Research 创始人兼首席执行官 Adam Parker 周二在 CNBC 的“收盘钟”节目中表示。 “我认为这些大公司的盈利和现金流足够强劲，足以应对围绕此事发生的任何恐慌。”

最新的联邦公开市场委员会会议纪要将于周三下午发布。鉴于央行内部分歧严重，投资者可能会密切关注会议纪要。在 7 月份的会议上，三名反对者投票支持加息，投资者将寻求更多细节。

本周零售业盈利仍将继续，塔吉特 (Target)、TJX 和 Lowe's 将于周三开盘前发布财报。 Analog Devices 也报道了这一情况。

查看盘后成为头条新闻的公司。

Toll Brothers — 这家豪华住宅建筑商的股价下跌 0.3%。 Toll Brothers 表示，预计第四季度的交付量将在 3,450 辆至 3,550 辆之间，而 StreetAccount 的普遍预期为 3,508 辆。该公司公布第三季度每股收益为 2.97 美元，营收为 26.5 亿美元。伦敦证券交易所集团 (LSEG) 调查的分析师预计每股收益为 2.93 美元，营收为 26.1 亿美元。

title: OpenAI 推出 ChatGPT 为青少年提供“更强大的内置安全保护”体验
content:
OpenAI 于周二发布了针对青少年的 ChatGPT，这是一种专门为 18 岁以下用户提供的聊天机器人体验，该公司称其旨在包括“更强大的内置安全保护”。

针对青少年的 ChatGPT 建立在 OpenAI 去年推出的多项功能的基础上，其中包括学习模式，旨在帮助学生逐步解决问题，以及帮助学生解决问题。预测和许多家长控制。

新的青少年体验包括一系列教育功能，包括作业提醒、测验和学习可视化以及学习时间，家长或青少年可以确定默认情况下何时开启学习模式。 OpenAI 表示，ChatGPT for Teens 还增加了适合年龄的保护措施，旨在减少接触不适合发育或有害内容的机会。

“青少年应该能够使用人工智能来学习、创造和探索，”OpenAI 在一份新闻稿中表示。 “但这种访问应该附带反映他们发展阶段的保护措施，加强现实世界的关系，并支持随着时间的推移健康使用。”

OpenAI 的 ChatGPT for Teens 体验的推出正值 Metais 启动一项高风险试验，以确定它是否会促进青少年和儿童的成瘾行为。这场审判可能会让 Meta 损失数千亿美元的损失，涉及 29 名州总检察长的联盟，他们于 2023 年对该公司提起了统一诉讼。

OpenAI 还面临着对其安全实践的审查。

6 月，佛罗里达州总检察长 James Uthmeier 对 OpenAI 及其首席执行官 Sam Altman 提起诉讼，指控该公司在知情的情况下发布了可能伤害用户的不安全产品。据报道，几天后，州检察官联盟对该公司展开调查。 OpenAI 在当时的一份声明中告诉 CNBC，它打算与这些官员“建设性地接触”。

今年 9 月，美国联邦贸易委员会对包括 OpenAI 和 Meta 在内的七家公司发起了调查，以了解他们的 AI 聊天机器人如何可能对儿童和青少年产生负面影响。

OpenAI 还面临着多起过失致人死亡诉讼，这些诉讼指控 ChatGPT 导致用户产生有害的妄想，在某些情况下，自杀。

如果您有自杀念头或陷入困境，请联系自杀与危机生命热线 988，寻求训练有素的顾问的支持和帮助。

注意：前 OpenAI 研究员表示，人工智能公司正处于“生存竞赛”中

title: 美国航空将在美国航班上恢复电视屏幕
content: Image source,Getty ImagesImage caption,American Airlines removed TVs from US domestic flights in 2017.ByFrancisco VelasquezBusiness reporter,ÂReporting fromNew YorkPublished1 hour agoAmerican Airlines wants its flyers to have screens â and not just the ones its passengers bring on board with them.The carrier says it will restore seatback displays across its domestic fleet, reversing a years-long strategy of removing them from most US routes.The company is also adding more premium seats, saying the changes are aimed at improving the travel experience and boosting revenue. American Airlines says the upgrades form part of a wider cabin investment announced this week.Its move follows years of complaints from passengers, who said that relying on personal devices left them with drained batteries, awkward viewing angles, and patchy Wi-Fi.It also comes as US carriers try to steady demand in a cooling market.American Airlines spent much of the past decade phasing out seatback screens from its Boeing 737s and Airbus A320-family jets, arguing that most travellers preferred to stream entertainment on their own devices.The airline also said removing built-in displays reduced weight and maintenance costs at a time when carriers were focused on efficiency.But the strategy left the carrier out of step with competitors like Delta and United, which have invested heavily in onboard entertainment to support a more premium cabin experience.JetBlue, meanwhile, has kept seatback TVs. Analysts say those choices have helped shift passenger expectations, making screens feel less like a luxury and more like a standard feature on many US flights."The long pull in the tent is technology," Raymond James analyst Savanthi Syth told the BBC, noting that Delta was the first major US carrier to introduce a basic economy fare and has continued adding new products since.Syth said those early moves put Delta further along in its "commercial journey", and the pace at which an airline introduces new offerings often depends on how developed its strategy already is.As technology improves â with lighter hardware, lower power use, and cheaper installation â screens have become easier for airlines to justify. American Airlines says it will roll out the new displays as quickly as possible, with full installation expected by early next decade.Its reversal suggests the carrier is trying to stay competitive and consistent, betting that more reliable onboard amenities will help it win customers while still appealing to budget-conscious travellers.Related topicsAir travelUnited StatesCompanies

title: 据报道，特朗普和卡尼正在就对加拿大商品征收新的 50% 关税进行谈判
content:
根据周二的各种新闻报道，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普正在与加拿大总理马克·卡尼重新进行贸易谈判，距离美国对曲棍球杆、葡萄酒和一系列其他加拿大进口产品征收 50% 的关税仅剩几个小时。

据彭博社报道，特朗普和卡尼周一晚间发表了讲话，并将于周二再次发表讲话。据福克斯商业报道，两国领导人周一晚间的会谈并未说服特朗普推迟即将实施的报复性关税。白宫没有立即回应 CNBC 的置评请求。

新关税将于周三生效，除非达成协议推迟或取消。商界领袖警告说，仅这一威胁就已经产生了巨大的不确定性，并已经影响了销售。

如果没有达成任何协议，这些关税将成为特朗普对加拿大征收的最新进口关税，特朗普是一位热衷于利用关税保护国内产业和增加政府收入的人。这些国家长期以来一直是亲密盟友和顶级贸易伙伴。

上个月公布了 50% 的关税，以回应特朗普政府所谓的加拿大在汽车、酒精和乳制品行业的贸易歧视。

这些关税是根据 1930 年关税法第 338 条征收的，这是一项大萧条时期的法律，几十年来很少被援引，而且一直被忽视。

新关税涵盖根据美国贸易代表办公室的数据，价值约 200 亿美元的加拿大进口产品。

虽然这只是美国去年从加拿大进口的 3,820 亿美元的一小部分，但目标产品的高税率仍可能对加拿大卖家构成重大挑战。

“50% 的关税本质上使产品销售到特定市场变得不经济，”加拿大独立企业联合会主席 Dan Kelly 在接受采访时表示CNBC 凯利表示，该组织 103,000 名成员中的许多成员表示，如果实施新关税，可能“导致他们在美国的销售陷入停滞”。他补充说，一些企业报告称，美国买家因预期新关税而推迟了未来的订单。

特朗普已对加拿大及其特定出口产品征收各种关税，包括金属、木材和汽车零部件。特朗普还因涉嫌贩毒问题对加拿大征收高额关税，但最高法院在 2 月份驳回了这些关税。

但凯利表示，338 条款关税“确实打击了加拿大和美国之间小企业贸易的核心”，因为许多目标产品都是以消费者为导向的。

“这对大量加拿大企业来说非常令人担忧，”他说。

一些特朗普政府对加拿大征收的关税包括对符合北美三边贸易协议（即 USMCA）的商品的豁免。

上个月，特朗普政府表示不会续签该贸易协议，引发了一系列年度审查，引发了对该条约未来的质疑。

美国商会美洲区高级副会长尼尔·赫林顿 (Neil Herrington) 在周二上午的一份声明中表示，新的更高关税“将损害双方利益”经济，增加美国家庭的成本，进一步扰乱关键的供应链，并使依赖贸易的 1300 万个美国就业岗位面临风险”。

title: 苹果彻底改革欧洲应用商店费用以解决支付冲突
content:
苹果周二宣布，欧盟的替代第三方应用商店将收取 5% 的应用内购买佣金，这家 iPhone 制造商表示，这将“解决”因实施欧洲数字市场法案而与监管机构之间的分歧。

根据新规则，使用苹果系统通过苹果应用商店购买的应用将支付 26% 的数字商品和服务佣金。使用自己的支付处理系统并直接接受信用卡的应用程序将向苹果支付 20% 的费用。链接到网站完成购买的应用程序将收取 15% 的费用，通过第三方应用商店或网络分发的应用程序将收取 5% 的费用，苹果称之为“核心技术委员会”。通过参加各种苹果计划，一些费用可以减半。

它是苹果去年提出的更复杂系统的替代品。新的费用等级将于 10 月 1 日生效。

从历史上看，Apple 对所有 iPhone 应用内购买收取 30% 或 15% 的费用，并要求所有非企业 iPhone 应用程序通过其 App Store 安装。但苹果的 App Store 模式在过去十年中一直在全球范围内受到诉讼和政府监管机构的攻击，批评者称其垄断了 iPhone 软件，并通过收费压榨开发者和用户。

苹果辩称，其 App Store 和应用内购买要求旨在增强信任和安全性，并强制解决安全和不当应用问题。

欧盟委员会于 2022 年通过了《数字市场法案》，要求像苹果这样的“看门人”开放市场其 App Store——以及 Siri 等其他 Apple 服务和产品——向第三方提供。但苹果公司与欧盟委员会就该公司的应用程序商店提案存在摩擦，苹果公司面临巨额罚款。

只有少数地区要求苹果公司启用可以销售 iPhone 应用程序的第三方应用程序商店，而欧洲是唯一用户可以从网络安装 iPhone 软件的地区。日本和巴西也要求第三方应用商店。

在美国，作为旷日持久的 Epic Games 诉讼的一部分，苹果正在努力限制用户链接到网络支付。它最近提议对美国的链接支付收取 15% 的佣金。

苹果表示，其周二的提议解决了与欧盟委员会在此事上的分歧。它还表示，它与欧盟委员会合作实施儿童安全措施，包括对某些应用内购买增加家长限制。

根据摩根士丹利的一份报告，苹果从其 App Store 中获得了大量收入，该收入计入其盈利的服务部门，但它没有强调 App Store 是最近一个季度服务增长的主要推动力，这是自 2023 年以来的首次。首席财务官 Kevan Parekh 在 7 月份与分析师的电话会议中指出，移动游戏速度较慢以及其他影响 App Store 表现的因素。

“请记住，我们还对某些国家/地区的 App Store 业务模式进行了一些更改，”Parekh 说道。
