title: 分析：随着华尔街等待沃什，债券市场压力正在挤压主街
content:
There's something telling in how the smart money on Wall Street has started to think about socialism. The moral of the story isn't really about socialism, though, but about the very real pain in store for American households from thebond marketif the actually-in-charge capitalists don't get their act together.

The idea is that socialists are on the rise, but the problem will be self-correcting because the national debt is so crushing it will force whoever's on top to deal with it.

"A democratic socialist, motivated by hatred of inequality, may be just determined enough to stake his or her political career on the idea that America can finally stomach some tax hikes," write Matt Gertken and Yushu Ma, analysts at research firm BCA, in a recent client note.

Whether that is true about socialism — who knows?

But the bond market is already becoming a check on Americans' livelihoods, with the capitalists firmly in charge. A sell-off in recent days has been triggered by an unlucky confluence of events and egged on, perhaps inadvertently, by the new Federal Reserve chairman,Kevin Warsh. That points to the conclusion that the pain for Main Street is likely to remain intense for the foreseeable future, even as Wall Street continues to prosper.

Bond traders have spent the summer selling off long-term U.S. government debt, resulting in a sharp steepening of the yield curve. The short end of the curve tends to follow the Federal Reserve'spolicy rate, while the long end reflects bets on growth and inflation. And while the Fed hasn't budged under Warsh, the market's view about the long end has gotten a lot more muddled lately.

The spread between2-yearand10-yearTreasuries has grown by nearly 29 basis points since June 24, according to FactSet data, a large gain in a short period. (One basis point equals 0.01%.) That was driven primarily by an increase in the 10-year, which traded above 4.7% on Tuesday.

Yields near 5% tend to provoke angst on Wall Street, because they allow investors to earn an alternative robust, risk-free return. Still, a sell-off would have to be deep to reset the economy's winners and losers. TheS&P 500has returned a cumulative 77% over the past three years, according to FactSet data. Stock holdings are concentrated among the wealthiest Americans.

Meanwhile, Treasury yields are dragging on Main Street. A swath of consumer debt is heavily influenced by the 10-year yield, including mortgages. A 30-year mortgage will now cost a typical purchaser 6.75%.

Frustrated home-buyers who want to know why buying is so tough won't find an easy answer.

The clearest trigger for the run-up in bond yields has been the Iran war. Oil is only trickling out of the Middle East, and U.S. refineries are running near maximum capacity. A gallon of diesel cost $5.46 on Tuesday, up 48% from a year ago, according to AAA data.

Add to the mix what seems to be an insatiable demand for debt by tech companies to builddata centers and other infrastructure for artificial intelligence. That competes with government bonds for investors' interest.

Supply-chain bottlenecks for chips and an aging electricity grid have led to price spikes. Technology that was for decades a contribution to slowing inflation has in recent years flipped toraising prices in aggregate.

Investors' inflation expectations measured by 5-year breakevens are essentially flat, according to LSEG data. That is keeping a floor under the long end of bond yields.

Economists can argue about how to weigh these and other factors. But finger-pointing about exactly what triggered the sell-off "misses the point in my opinion," writes Robin Brooks, senior fellow for economic studies at the centrist think tank the Brookings Institution, in a newsletter Tuesday.

"When you have a lot of debt and run unsustainably large budget deficits, you're extremely vulnerable to any old shock that comes along. It's not about the shock, but - instead - the mess we are making of fiscal policy on a global scale," Brooks writes.

He is looking at global markets, but there is little dispute that the U.S. is a mess.

The U.S. budget deficit is set to come in at around 6.4% of gross domestic product, based on the Congressional Budget Office's recent estimate that thedeficit will hit $2.1 trillionfor the fiscal year through September.

The Trump administration has said that some of the increase in spending is due to the one-time military necessity of the Iran war, and that lower-income households have seen wage increases recently. But it has no obvious plan to cut deficits.

Warsh, the new Fed chairman, has expressed some sympathy for regular Americans battered by high interest rates. His view is that financial conditions are restrictive on Main Street — particularly in housing — but clearly loose on Wall Street.

The question now is whether Warsh will do anything about it.

Warsh in July seemed to welcome the rise in bond yields, noting that they have risen in real and nominal terms while the Fed kept its rates steady. "At some level, we haven't done much in 42 days. The markets have done quite a bit," Warsh said.

Warsh's seeming acceptance of higher rates prompted traders to push rates still higher.

He has also argued that the Fed helped juice Wall Street by putting trillions of dollars worth of Treasurys and mortgage securities on its balance sheet in the years since the financial crisis. But he is yet to convince the rest of the Fed to go along with reversing that, and in the short term, a reduction in the Fed's balance-sheet holdings would put more upward pressure on long-term treasuries and mortgages.

Warsh will have an opportunity to nudge the market in a new direction, if he so chooses, when he takes the stage at a closely watched central bankers' conference in Jackson Hole, Wyo., on Aug. 28. He is likely to talk about the state of the economy and how he sees the relationship between the bond market and the Fed. His views on the balance sheet will likely have to wait until a Fed task force on that issue reports back in a few months.

Warsh's views in Jackson Hole may help to stem the bond-market selloff and ease the pain on Main Street. But one speech can only do so much, and the Fed can't do anything directly about the balance of government spending and revenue.

That, of course, is why Wall Street is thinking ahead. At some point, the bond sell-off will likely hit a point where prices are so attractive that investors will swoop in and start buying again. When the buyers come back, yields will fall. Markets have been through this cycle repeatedly in recent years, with the 10-year yield edging up toward 5%, threatening stocks, and then tumbling back down again.

That cycle may not add up to a financial crisis. But unless it eases, it will almost certainly fuel a continuing, slow-burn political crisis.

If capitalists don't seize their moment, the socialists will.

title: 迪士尼和美国广播公司起诉特朗普媒体监管机构，要求其停止提前更新许可证
content: 图片来源，盖蒂图片社作者：布兰登·德雷农 (Brandon Drenon) 和伯恩德·德布斯曼 (Bernd Debusmann Jr)，白宫记者 38 分钟前发布 迪士尼和美国广播公司 (ABC) 已提起诉讼，阻止特朗普政府启动早期许可证更新程序，称该网络因其社论内容而受到不公平的攻击。“政府的审查制度非常不美国，”诉讼称。 “此案涉及政府为此所做的持续努力。” 该诉讼称，联邦通信委员会（政府的媒体监管机构）面临压力，要求提前几年更新广播许可证。据称，这一推动源于唐纳德·特朗普总统的投诉，并在他的指导下进行。FCC 主席布伦丹·卡尔表示，续订请求的重点是“公共利益”，而不是报复。“如果广播公司不喜欢这样，那也没关系，”卡尔在 7 月份告诉 CNBC。“他们可以成为有线频道，他们可以成为播客，他们可以在线播放。但如果你想在公众广播中脱颖而出，你就必须遵守这些规定“BBC 已联系 FCC 征求意见。迪士尼及其拥有和经营的八家电视台是周二针对 FCC 及其主席提起的诉讼的原告。FCC 在 4 月份下令为迪士尼旗下的 ABC 电视台续订许可证。迪士尼此前曾因涉嫌多样性、公平和包容性 (DEI) 做法以及 ABC 的日间脱口秀节目《The View》而受到调查。但 FCC 提前更新许可证的通知是在一天后发出的。美国广播公司 (ABC) 的深夜主持人吉米·金梅尔 (Jimmy Kimmel) 拿第一夫人梅拉尼娅·特朗普 (Melania Trump) 开玩笑。在诉讼中，迪士尼称 FCC 的这项命令是“史无前例的”，并称在此之前，该委员会已有 50 多年没有要求提前续签。诉讼称，“政府通过联邦通信委员会采取行动，对 ABC 发起了报复行动，原因只有一个：它不赞成 ABC 的广播内容。”诉讼称。它引用了特朗普自己的社交媒体帖子：证据，其中包括特朗普抱怨 ABC 对他的报道“几乎 100% 负面”。在同一篇社交媒体帖子中，特朗普还质疑他们的广播许可证是否应该“终止”，并回答了他自己的问题：“我说，是的！”。在 FCC 主席卡尔的压力下，迪士尼于 2025 年 9 月停止了金梅尔的播出，因为他发表了有关保守派活动人士和特朗普盟友查理·柯克被谋杀的言论。但金梅尔很快又回到了自己的角色。公众对涉嫌违反言论自由的行为表示强烈反对，其中包括共和党参议员特德·克鲁兹。FCC 给了 ABC 和迪士尼 30 天的时间来提交申请，据诉讼中的原告称，“通常需要几个月的时间来准备”。诉讼还指出，FCC 从未要求同一广播网络共同拥有的一组电视台提前提出续约申请。ABC 和迪士尼已要求法院“迅速举行听证会”并颁发临时限制令。图片来源，盖蒂图片社图片说明，布伦丹卡尔与特朗普总统（资料图片）卡尔曾被特朗普总统誉为“言论自由斗士”，但长期以来，他发现自己处于政府与媒体之间日益激烈的好斗关系的中心。甚至在去年 1 月在委员会任职多年后，卡尔就明确表示，他将对自己的权力采取更广泛的看法。美国广播公司尤其多次引起卡尔的愤怒。 2025 年 9 月，喜剧演员吉米·金梅尔在柯克被谋杀后发表评论后，他公开威胁要对那些没有对喜剧演员吉米·金梅尔进行反击的媒体公司采取行动。“我们可以通过简单的方法或困难的方法来做到这一点，”卡尔告诉保守派播客本尼·约翰逊。 “坦率地说，这些公司可以找到一种方法来改变行为，并在金梅尔问题上采取行动，或者你知道 FCC 未来还会有更多工作。” 早些时候，特朗普成功起诉 ABC 新闻和乔治·斯特凡诺普洛斯诽谤，此前电视主播表示总统在 E·让·卡罗尔案中被发现“对强奸负有责任”，而不是性虐待和诽谤。ABC 解决了此案，并同意为他的总统基金会和博物馆支付 1500 万美元，加上100万美元的法律费用。相关话题迪士尼媒体美国更多关于这个故事FCC做什么——它可以撤销电视网络的许可证吗？发布2025年9月20日美国监管机构将在吉米·金梅尔关于梅拉尼娅·特朗普的玩笑后审查迪士尼广播许可证发布2025年9月20日参议员特德·克鲁兹称美国广播监管机构对吉米·金梅尔的行为就像“黑手党”发布2025年9月20日

title: 受石油、人工智能和通胀影响，全球借贷成本再创新高
content: 图片来源，Getty Images作者：Michael RaceBusiness记者，纽约报道34分钟前发布由于对通胀、政府债务水平和人工智能(AI)支出的担忧，全球一些最大经济体的长期借贷成本创下新高。美国30年以上借贷利率周二触及5.33%，为2007年6月以来最高，同时英国长期债务达到5.85%。德国和日本也有类似的举措。债券的利率（债务的一种）被称为收益率，可以直接影响消费者支付抵押贷款、汽车贷款和信用卡的借贷成本。油价上涨是近期债券收益率飙升的主要推动因素，因为投资者担心通胀可能再次飙升。如果发生这种情况，各国央行可能会选择提高利率来冷却通胀。周二，全球油价基准布伦特原油价格突破 90 美元。最近的激增是在唐纳德·特朗普总统威胁美国盟友阿曼，如果它“妨碍”与伊朗重新开放霍尔木兹海峡航道的谈判，就对其进行轰炸。美国和阿曼分别与伊朗政府进行谈判，以重新开放对全球石油供应和其他贸易至关重要的关键通道。由于美以与伊朗的战争，该海峡基本上关闭了近六个月，导致石油供应中断，导致价格上涨。汽车燃料成本上升，全球油价上涨可能导致价格全面上涨，因为企业将面临的更高费用转嫁给消费者，从而推高通货膨胀。石油是商业的关键因素。货物通常是通过卡车或货车运输的。牛津经济研究院首席分析师约翰·卡纳万 (John Canavan) 向 BBC 表示，油价上涨带来的通胀风险、高水平的政府债务以及人工智能投资的巨额资金以及何时能获得回报的不确定性，这些都导致借贷成本上升。他表示，这可能会导致消费者的抵押贷款利率和汽车贷款借贷成本上升。他警告说，更高的收益率意味着企业可能需要支付更多的钱来借贷，他说：“这会增加整体通胀的影响。”他补充说，从长远来看，通胀上升可能会减缓经济增长。如果通胀很高或预计未来通胀会升高，债券投资者通常会要求更高的回报或收益率。政府和企业出售债券（本质上是借条）以筹集支出资金，并支付利息。卡纳万表示，除了通胀担忧之外，世界各地的债券投资者也出现了“抵制”。英国的财政状况和借贷水平导致首相安迪·伯纳姆向债券市场保证，他致力于遵守政府现有的借贷限额，即财政规则。今年夏天，当他从凯尔·斯塔默爵士手中接过工党领导权时，借贷成本小幅上升。在就财政规则作出承诺之前，投资者曾认为伯纳姆更有可能提高英国本已较高的公共债务水平。卡纳万表示，最近几周企业借贷“创纪录的速度”也推动了美国的长期借贷成本，这些借贷主要用于人工智能和数据中心的开发和建设。然而，由于投入人工智能的数千亿美元以及潜在风险的不确定性，投资者要求更高的贷款回报。 Bokeh Capital Partners 首席投资官 Kim Forrest 表示：“这让人们感到不安，因为这预示着环境将更加紧张，借钱的成本也会更高。特别是在整个人工智能领域，还款时间不确定，这导致投资者环境紧张。”

title: 数据中心、加密货币和税收修订成为周二初选的焦点
content:
Primary electionseason continues Tuesday as voters inAlaska,FloridaandWyominghead to the polls to choose their party's candidates for November'smidterm elections, which are less than three months away.

The November midterms will determine control ofCongressfor the remainder of PresidentDonald Trump's term. If Democrats, who are ahead in the polls, capture one or both chambers of Congress, it would severely limit legislation for the next two years and potentially increase oversight of the White House and industry.

"The decline in President Trump's approval ratings across a range of issues has increased Democratic prospects," said one recent analysis from TD Cowen. "Divided government could leave policy in a gridlock."

Tuesday's elections come in the wake of contests in Michigan, Wisconsin and Minnesota over the past several weeks, which were closely watched on the Democratic side as the party grapples with whether to lean further to the left or track toward the center after crushing losses in 2024. In Senate primaries, Democrats nominated progressivesAbdul El-Sayedin Michigan andPeggy Flanaganin Minnesota, but democratic socialist Francesca Hong fell short in the Wisconsin gubernatorial primary to centrist David Crowley.

Progressive candidates have surged in primaries across the country, pushing a platform of implementing universal healthcare known as Medicare for All, taxing the wealthy and taking a tougher tack against corporations.

Top issues in Tuesday's primaries include data centers in Florida, cryptocurrency in Wyoming, and taxes in Alaska.

Alaska voters head to the polls Tuesday for a set of contests headlined by a Senate race for the seat currently occupied by Sen. Dan Sullivan, R-Alaska. The primary contest in Alaska is not broken down by party and will instead see the top four vote-getters advance to a ranked-choice general election in November.

Sullivan, who is running for reelection, is facing a tough challenge from former Democratic Rep. Mary Peltola. The former congresswoman lost reelection in 2024, but won statewide in Alaska twice in 2022 — giving Democrats hope she can oust Sullivan.

The Cook Political Report rates the Alaska Senate race as a toss-up, and it has become a key contest in the battle for control of the Senate.

Peltola, unlike Flanagan and El-Sayed, is running a centrist campaign. She's pushing for targeted tax credits for Alaska oil and gas refineries and revisions to permitting so energy projects can move ahead more quickly. Borrowing from the left, however, Peltola is calling for the elimination of federal income tax for Alaskans making less than $92,000 per year, and paying for it by increasing taxes on millionaires and billionaires.

Peltola has also rejected ties to the national Democratic Party — recently moving to distance herself from the endorsement of former Vice PresidentKamala Harris, the Democratic presidential nominee in 2024, according toThe New York Times.

Sullivan, a Marine veteran, has represented Alaska in the Senate since 2015. He serves on the committees on armed services, commerce, environment and public works, and veterans affairs. He is generally a reliable vote for Republicans, in contrast to his Alaska Republican counterpart, Sen. Lisa Murkowski, who is one of the Senate's usual swing votes.

Sullivan is endorsed by Trump, who carried the state by about 13 points in 2024.

Also figuring into Alaska's Senate primary is another Daniel Sullivan, a former teacher who has joined the race as a Republican and has the same name as the incumbent senator. Sen. Sullivan has accused the other Sullivan of being a Democratic plant meant to confuse voters and potentially siphon votes away from his campaign. That could matter in November if both Sullivans make it through the primary.

Florida is holding gubernatorial and Senate primaries Tuesday, with data centers becoming a top issue among voters, according to a recentPoliticoreport. Hyperscalers have reportedly struggled to get projects across the finish line in the state due to pushback.

Many candidates have raced to distance themselves from the facilities that drive artificial intelligence as voters recoil from increased utility bills.

Rep. Byron Donalds, R-Fla., is the Trump-endorsed candidate running to replace Gov. Ron DeSantis, a Republican who is term-limited. Donalds is a heavy favorite in the Republican gubernatorial primary field, which also includes Lt. Gov. Jay Collins and investor James Fishback.

AI interests have spent big backing Donalds,according to Bloomberg.

Donalds has called for data center builders to pay their own way in the state, similar to the White House'sRatepayer Protection Pledgethat sought to ensure hyperscalers are paying for any increases in utility bills. His campaign has denied that campaign contributions from Big Tech will sway his support for data centers as governor.

DeSantis has signed strict legislation into law on the issue, including a prohibition on data centers passing on costs to ratepayers and new authority for local communities to reject data centers from being built.

Collins, meanwhile, has called for a "Florida Strong standard [that] requires operators to fund their own project infrastructure and meet Florida's water, reliability, and ratepayer terms, so families and seniors are never stuck subsidizing Big Tech's power demand."

And Fishback has gone even further, saying he would ban data centers in "all 67 counties by preventing county commissions from approving them in the first place."

Democrats have struggled mightily in Florida in the Trump era. But they're hoping that their luck will turn this year as former Republican-turned-independent Rep. David Jolly campaigns for the party's nomination for governor. Recent general election polling has found Jolly down but within striking distance of Donalds.

Florida is also holding a Senate primary. Sen. Ashley Moody, R-Fla., is running for a full term after replacing now-Secretary of State Marco Rubio. She's expected to face the winner of a Democratic primary field that includes Army veteran Alex Vindman and state politician Angela Nixon.

Wyoming voters are heading to the polls to decide the successor to Republican Sen.Cynthia Lummis, who will retire at the end of her term. Lummis, known as the "crypto queen," has been a key player in pushing legislation related to cryptocurrency.

Rep. Harriet Hageman, R-Wyo., has secured Trump's endorsement and is the favorite to succeed Lummis.

Hageman has voted solidly in favor of crypto, but has not made it a top issue like Lummis did. Instead, Hageman has focused heavily on curbing federal regulation and resource issues.

A Democrat has not won statewide office in Wyoming since 2006, when former Gov. Dave Freudenthal was reelected. The Democratic field for the Senate race includes state Rep. James Byrd.

title: 美国国税局明确了“加班不征税”的扣除规则。工人需要了解什么
content:
Workers who are eligible for a federaltaxbreak related to their overtime pay may have an easier time claiming it for the 2026 tax year than they did on their 2025 returns.

The IRS hasupdated its frequently asked questionsabout the "no tax on overtime" deduction to clarify and expand the information it has provided. There was some confusion about the deduction when 2025 tax returns were filed earlier this year, experts say.

"'No tax on overtime' can fit on a bumper sticker, but all of the terms and conditions that apply … naturally led to lots of questions from workers andemployersabout what kind of overtime is eligible and what kind of reporting is required of employers," said Andrew Lautz, senior director of federal policy for the Tax Foundation, a nonpartisan research group. "Now there are a lot more details."

Notably, employers will be required to include the information on workers' W-2s for the 2026 tax year. This means taxpayers won't be responsible for determining eligibility or calculating their own deduction as many were for their 2025 return.

"It was complicated this filing season, and I expect employer reporting will make things less complicated for workers," Lautz said.

The no tax on overtime tax break was included in PresidentDonald Trump'sOne Big Beautiful Bill Act, which was signed into law in July 2025. It was one of several new temporary deductions that taxpayers may be eligible for — alongside those forauto loan interest,tip incomeand an extra deduction fortaxpayers ages 65 or older. All four are in effect for tax years 2025 through 2028.

For the overtime tax break, eligible workers can deduct a portion — up to $12,500 for single tax filers or $25,000 for married couples filing jointly — of qualifying overtime on their tax return. The deduction applies to overtime pay covered under theFair Labor Standards Act, which says nonexemptemployeesmust be paid at least 1.5 times their normal pay rate for time worked beyond 40 hours per week.

However, the deduction is only for the "overtime premium" — the one-half portion of that 1.5 rate. For illustration: If a covered worker's regular hourly rate is $40, and their overtime rate is $60 per hour, only the $20 premium — the amount above the regular rate — counts toward the deduction. The tax break starts phasing out at incomes of $150,000 for single taxpayers and $300,000 for joint tax returns.

The updated IRS FAQs include the requirement that employers put the amount eligible for the deduction on workers' W-2s, in box 12 using a "TT" code. While it's possible for an independent contractor to receive a 1099-MISC or 1099-NEC that includes eligible overtime pay, it would be "rare" circumstances causing that, according to the IRS.

The FAQs also clarify that if state law or union agreement requires overtime pay that is different from the FLSA, only the portion mandated under the FLSA qualifies — generally the extra half in the 1.5 times pay rule — for the deduction.

More than 29 million taxpayers claimed the deduction for overtime wages in the latest tax season through the April 15 filing deadline, according to aJuly 2 releasefrom the Treasury Department. The average deduction was above $3,100, the release says. Additionally, 75% of those filers had income under $100,000 and 96% had income under $200,000.

For tax year 2025, the Treasury Department and IRSwaived the employer requirementto separately report the amount eligible for the deduction because systems and procedures weren't yet in place to capture that information, and the necessary IRS tax forms had not been updated to include it. As a result, many workers had to calculate their own eligible amounts using payroll statements or a final pay stub for the year.

"We had to use people's pay stubs … and make a best guesstimate as to what the amount of qualified overtime would be," said Tom O'Saben, director of tax content and government relations for the National Association of Tax Professionals.

"All things being equal, it's entirely possible that the deduction we take in 2026 for overtime could be less than what was taken in 2025 because those calculations could have been wrong," O'Saben said.

Even if the overtime pay deduction information does appear on your W-2, it's worth making sure it's accurate.

"I'm going to ask my clients to still bring those pay stubs, and let's spend a few minutes to [check] that number and see if it's accurate," O'Saben said.

If it's not, the worker will need to ask for a corrected W-2.

"If the worker believes that an error has been made in the information their employer provided them for overtime compensation, whether that's the employer put too much or too little, it's on the worker to request an updated W-2," Lautz said.

"If you see a mistake, you can't say 'oh I'm going to correct that myself' … and claim a different deduction amount," he said.

title: Hims & Hers 首席执行官表示 FTC 诉讼误解了公司的运作方式
content:
Hims & Hers首席执行官安德鲁·杜杜姆 (Andrew Dudum) 在联邦贸易委员会对其数据共享做法提起诉讼时为远程医疗公司进行了辩护。

在周二播出的一次内容广泛的独家采访中，杜杜姆声称这些指控源于对该公司如何改变医疗保健的误解。

“我只能说，你知道什么时候你正在改变对医疗保健等传统系统如何运作的基本理解，并且你正在数字生态系统中重建它，”他在 CNBC 的“Squawk Box”节目中告诉 Andrew Ross Sorkin。 “我认为人们需要时间来理解如何以正确的方式做到这一点，我们与联邦贸易委员会合作多年，引导他们完成这一点。我认为最终他们想要的更多是一个标题，而不是真正的协议。”

7 月，联邦贸易委员会、洛杉矶县和犹他州对 Hims & Hers 提起诉讼。它指责该公司与 Meta 和 Snap 等广告商共享用户健康信息，在客户与医疗保健提供者交谈之前就收取处方费，并使取消订阅变得困难。

Dudum 为这家远程医疗提供商的商业模式进行了辩护，称其建立在增加获得医疗服务的基础上。

“我们是积极的颠覆者。我们正视这一点，我们愿意这样做。但总是当我们相信这符合人们及其利益的最佳利益时。” Dudum 说道。

Hims & Hers 首席执行官还对公司从复合药物向品牌 GLP-1 药物的过渡发表了看法。近年来，当流行的肥胖和减肥药物短缺时，该公司可以合法地以折扣价销售山寨版本。

供应恢复后，诺和诺德起诉 Hims & Hers 专利侵权。今年 3 月，这家丹麦制药商放弃了诉讼，这家远程医疗公司同意在其平台上销售 Novo 的品牌药物。

这一决定是在 Novo 及其主要竞争对手礼来公司 (Eli Lilly) 降低 GLP-1 药物价格以自付费用的情况下做出的。

“最终，如果我们认为这对消费者最有利，我们将始终向该系统施加压力。当我们配制 GLP-1 时，没有负担得起的药物获得这些疗法，”杜杜姆说。 “现在，它在生态系统中的作用是向消费者和制药公司表明，这些药物可以以每个人都能负担得起的价格提供给消费者。”

Dudum 表示，他最终预计现金支付患者的价格将从现在的大约 150 美元到 200 美元降至每月 40 美元到 50 美元，具体取决于药物的形式。

Dudum 还表示，他相信人工智能将极大地改变医疗保健行业，公司正在增加投资，以最终实现“人工智能原生。” Dudum 表示 Hims & Hers 正在放弃第三方人工智能代理，转而在内部构建一切。

“独立于闭环数据集的核心基础模型没有那么有价值。这是我的诚实观点，”Dudum 说。 “像 Hims & Hers 这样的医疗保健系统中拥有的闭环数据就是资产。”

title: Sea Ray 母公司 Brunswick 押注人工智能导航和新的收入来源，以帮助遏制船舶销售
content:
Brunswick Corp. 是全球船舶制造和水上娱乐领域的领导者，正在依靠先进技术来帮助解决销售停滞问题。

Sea Ray、Boston Whaler 和其他船舶品牌的母公司表示，先进的导航技术和自主入坞可以降低在拥挤的码头操纵船舶的复杂性。

赌注是双重的：说服潜在买家进入一个一直以来都处于困境的市场。低迷——预计到 2026 年新船的零售销售将保持低迷——并通过技术和软件销售增加售后市场和经常性收入。

Brunswick 的产品组合远远超出了船舶品牌。其 Navico Group 销售船用电子产品和技术，而 Mercury Marine 则供应发动机并维持零部件业务。

Brunswick 目前大约 60% 的收入来自售后市场或经常性收入，Roth Capital Partners 分析师 Scott Stember 表示，这种组合使该公司在新船销售之外具有有意义的曝光度。

Brunswick 告诉投资者，预计年销量将达到 145,000 至 160,000 艘到 2030 年，Roth 认为，今年美国零售销量估计不足 135,000 艘船舶，需求将温和复苏。

不伦瑞克省最便宜的型号最能感受到需求疲软。

“我们看到优质船舶和我们所谓的核心产品组合非常有弹性，”首席执行官 David Foulkes 告诉 CNBC。 “我们看到的是价值船，它们通常更容易获得融资或更容易受到利率压力......它们的表现并不差，但它们的表现不如我们的一些更优质的产品。”

但 Brunswick 可以增加船上电子设备和技术的数量，即使售出的船只数量没有大幅增加。

例如，Navico 55% 的原始设备客户增加了他们的船舶数量。据该公司称，Navico 内容自 2023 年起。自 2025 年以来，Navico 已推出 30 多种新产品。

其中之一是 Simrad AutoCaptain，它可以帮助船舶导航和停靠。商业策略是有道理的：让船出海变得容易，更重要的是让船回来，你可能会卖掉一艘更大、更贵的船。该公司还围绕船创造了更多业务。

该战略的另一部分是自由船俱乐部 - 一种划船者乡村俱乐部，在全球各地设有分支机构。会员需缴纳费用和月费才能使用船只在任何地点进行水上活动。

Brunswick 在 8 月份的投资者日报告称，自 2019 年以来，该俱乐部的会员数量增加了两倍多，达到 63,000 多名会员。旅行和预订量增长了四倍，网络已扩展到 450 多个地点和约 5,000 艘船的船队。

与新船的周期性销售不同，Freedom Boat Club 完全属于不伦瑞克的经常性收入范围，俱乐部约 90% 的销售额为经常性收入，旅行次数比一年前增加了 10%，这表明消费者正在继续出海旅行即使新船销售仍然疲弱。

随着 Brunswick 制定了雄心勃勃的财务目标，但没有假设行业会回到繁荣时期，这种方法变得更加重要。

该公司的目标是到 2030 年收入达到 70 亿至 80 亿美元，营业利润率为 10% 至 13%，每股收益在 8 至 12 美元之间。

KeyBanc 对 Brunswick 给予行业权重评级管理层表示，管理层预计定价、更丰富的优质产品组合、市场份额的增长和新产品创新将有助于推动增长。

Roth 的股价目标价为 94 美元，他的看法更为乐观。 Stember 写道，Brunswick 在娱乐和休闲领域处于“独特的地位”，即使新船需求仅出现“温和/不显着”的复苏，Brunswick 也能实现有意义的盈利增长。

Brunswick 的股价目前约为每股 82 美元。

Brunswick 还试图通过将其来自中国的零部件减少多达 75% 并将关税风险削减 75% 来消除供应链风险。 70%。

Foulkes 表示，这使 Brunswick 比海外竞争对手更具优势。

当然，投资者会权衡先进技术、更高效的发动机以及来自 Freedom Boat Club 的经常性收入的总和是否能够保持利润持续增长，即使单位增长仍然充满挑战。

— CNBC 的 Ryan Ruggiero 对本报告作出了贡献。

title: 迪士尼旗下的美国广播公司 (ABC) 根据第一修正案对 FCC 提起诉讼
content:
迪士尼旗下的 ABC 已根据第一修正案对联邦通信委员会提起诉讼，称政府机构最近对该公司的调查是一次“报复行动”，因为其节目的性质一直批评唐纳德·特朗普总统。

该广播网络于周二向华盛顿特区的地方法院提起诉讼。

几个月前，FCC 启动了 ABC 一套提前续订计划。

然而，在电视主持人吉米·金梅尔 (Jimmy Kimmel) 在其广播网络播出的深夜节目中发表评论后不久，针对 ABC 的政治反弹再次出现，之后不久，这一早期审查程序就开始了。 ABC 还因其日间脱口秀节目《The View》而面临政府的批评。

ABC 的诉讼要求 FCC 停止其早期的广播续订程序。

FCC 没有立即回应对此诉讼发表评论的请求。

该机构于 4 月份启动了对 ABC 许可证的审查，比预定到期时间提前了数年。 ABC 早在 5 月份就在文件中表示，它提交申请是“为了回应 FCC 的非法、任意和违宪命令的抗议”。

FCC 主席 Brendan Carrt 告诉 CNBC，当时该机构的重点是迪士尼的 DEI 做法，并且早期许可证更新与第一修正案问题无关。

Carr 被特朗普任命领导旨在监管媒体和电信的联邦实体。行业。去年，ABC 开始对迪士尼电视台进行调查，理由是它们可能违反 1934 年《通信法》和 FCC 关于禁止非法歧视的规定。

周二，ABC 表示，它“继续面临来自政府的不可挽回的伤害”，而政府“一直在通过 FCC 采取行动”。

上周，迪士尼首席执行官乔什·达马罗 (Josh D'Amaro) 在 CNBC 节目中加强了该公司的立场。 ” 采访。

“我想你在我们向 FCC 提交的文件中看到了我们对此的立场很明确，”达马罗当时对 CNBC 的 Julia Boorstin 说道。 “我们在这方面非常有原则。我们将坚守我们所认为的新闻报道和诚信，我们不会被告知如何经营这方面的业务。”

达马罗于 3 月份从长期担任迪士尼首席执行官的鲍勃·艾格 (Bob Iger) 手中接任首席执行官。

上周，艾格同意与 Thrive Capital 创始人兼兄弟约书亚·库什纳 (Joshua Kushner) 一起购买 NBA 洛杉矶湖人队的多数股权。贾里德·库什纳 (Jared Kushner) 的妻子是特朗普的女儿伊万卡 (Ivanka)。

title: 由加密货币交易所 Kraken 构建的支付应用程序刚刚推出了现金返还借记卡，以吸引消费者钱包
content:
加密货币交易所 Kraken 制造商的一款支付应用程序正在推出一款返现美国借记卡，随着加密货币从一种资产类别发展成为主流金融产品的基础设施，该卡将在消费者钱包中争夺一席之地。

该卡名为 Krak Card，由同名附属货币应用程序发行，提供高达 2% 的现金或比特币返还，利率根据客户持有的资产价值而增加。奖励直接以金钱而非积分形式支付。

它还允许客户直接使用 600 多种货币和加密资产进行消费，并在购买时自动将他们选择的余额转换为美元。用户可以设置资产的支出顺序，并可以选择将单次购买分摊到多个余额中。

此举使 Krak 与支付和金融科技超级应用程序（包括 Block 的 CashApp、PayPal 的 Venmo、SoFi、Robinhood 和 Chime）进行更直接的竞争。随着加密货币越来越多地嵌入到更广泛的金融体系中，行业参与者正在竞相充当更广泛的金融产品的分销层。

Kraken 的机会不仅仅在于交换费，即客户使用其借记卡时产生的费用。 Krak 通过合作伙伴银行提供该卡，该银行发行该卡并受美国借记卡交换费限制。这些限制限制了可用于支持奖励的交易收入，这使得 2% 的奖励很难仅通过卡消费来提供资金。

Kraken 可能更感兴趣的是增加其可以捕获的每个客户的财务生命量，使用新的借记卡保留存款，推动支出并在其平台上保留更多客户资产。

Kraken 成立于 2011 年，历史上一直是为加密货币原生者提供服务的交易所。其核心用户群包括机构、交易公司、专业交易者和主动杠杆交易者，其许多零售用户可能已经交易加密货币多年（尽管该公司正试图通过其新重建的应用程序中的代理交易功能来扩大其用户群）。相比之下，Coinbase 将自己定位为加密货币的门户，而 Robinhood 则将自己定位为广泛投资的门户。

在加密货币的未来似乎不再那么“加密”的时候——也就是说，模因硬币的交易越来越少，股票、大宗商品、首次公开募股和美元的代币化程度越来越高——Kraken 似乎正在加倍强调其独特的加密原生身份。它的根源可以追溯到加密货币的早期，当时去中心化和财务自治是该运动的核心，随着行业的成熟，Kraken 并没有远离这种文化，而是似乎将其作为其品牌的决定性组成部分。

“人们对金融体系如何对待他们、对他们支付的费率、他们收取的费用以及奖励的实际运作方式失去了信任。他们这样做是对的，”Kraken 母公司 Payward 的联合首席执行官 Arjun Sethi 表示。在一份声明中。

借记卡是围绕美国消费者与他们可用的金融产品之间日益脱节而建立的。 Krak 委托对 2,000 多名美国成年人进行的一项全国调查显示，63% 的美国人表示，他们感到经济落后，而 60% 的人会转而使用借记卡，这种卡可以提供有意义的奖励，而不要求他们承担债务。

“几十年来，该系统一直在默默的补贴下运行：普通人的存款、费用和支出为回报提供资金，而这些回报很少回流到他们身上。旧的交易很简单：如果你想要奖励，你必须承担债务才能得到它们。”塞西说。 “Krak 卡将人们选择持有的任何东西转化为可以在任何地方消费的货币，并以现金而非积分的形式返还价值。”

除了加密货币交易之外，Kraken 还提供现货和衍生品交易、机构托管和代币化股票。它还拥有怀俄明州银行执照，并于今年早些时候成为第一家获得美联储主账户的加密公司，这意味着其银行子公司可以直接连接到美国核心支付轨道。

title: 根据《普林斯顿评论》，2026 年经济援助排名前 10 的大学——以及家庭实际支付的费用
content:
With some colleges now charging more than$100,000 a year, cost is the single biggest barrier to entry for prospective students,recent studies show.

But families don't often pay the sticker price. In fact, students and their parents spent closer to $35,000, on average, on college costs — including tuition, fees, books, room and board, technology and other expenses — during the 2025-26 academic year, according to Sallie Mae's recentHow America Pays for Collegereport.

In most cases, families tap savings and cobble together other resources to cover the tab, including scholarships, second jobs, and federal and privatestudent loans.

Of all possible sources, "merit aid is an underutilized resource," said Robert Franek, editor-in-chief at The Princeton Review. Beyond federal assistance from the U.S. Department of Education and state aid, many schools are increasingly offering students more scholarship funds.

"These are grants, money that students don't have to pay back," Franek said. "That is significant."

Between the 2014-15 and 2024-25 academic years, institutional grant aid rose by 24% to $85.1 billion. During 2024-25, institutional money accounted for about half of all grant aid for undergraduate and graduate students, according to the latest data available from the College Board, which trackstrends in college pricing and student aid.

Financial aidis increasingly influencing students' college decisions. Nearly nine in 10 students — 89% — said they would have chosen a different college for more scholarship aid, according to a new report by education software companyEllucian, based on a survey of more than 2,000 current and prospective college students in the U.S.

To that end,The Princeton Review ranked collegesby how generous their financial aid awards are and how satisfied students are with their packages. The 2027 edition of the company's "Best Colleges" guide is based on data from surveys of 170,000 students during the 2025-26 academic year. Sticker prices are based on the upcoming school year, as of June.

The colleges and universities that ranked highest on The Princeton Review's list successfully met students' growing need for assistance, Franek said.

"There is money out there, great big buckets of money," Franek said.

Washington and Lee University, for example, is the most expensive school on the list with an annual sticker price near six figures. However, the school's average need-based scholarship is nearly $72,000, which brings the total out-of-pocket cost down to around $25,000, according to The Princeton Review.

"Washington and Lee University delivers on its commitment to meet the full financial need of our students without loans, while also being need-blind in admissions and providing full-ride merit-based Johnson Scholarships to 10% of each entering class, thanks to the incredible generosity of our dedicated alumni," said Drewry Sackett, Washington and Lee's spokesperson.

title: 逆向投资者与大众投资者：一位交易员大量押注做空芯片股
content:
当谈到最重要的半导体行业的命运时，期权市场的交易者面临着一个典型的投资困境：随大流，还是大笔逆势投资？根据期权流向，人群正倾向于自四月份以来最严重的看涨。问题在于，周一整个市场最大的单一期权交易——价值 1.29 亿美元的交易，占 VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) 总溢价的三分之一以上——完全是看跌的。首先，人群：SMH 的未平仓看跌期权与看涨期权合约的比率周一下滑至 1.89，这是自 4 月初以来看涨期权的最大不平衡，并且从 6 月最后一周的高点 3.5 下降。该比率至少在一年内没有跌破 1.5，反映了对看跌期权作为多头股票头寸对冲工具的普遍需求。

未平仓利率的波动可以说是今年基础 ETF 价格的一个引人注目的指标。随着 SMH 势头放缓，交易员在 5 月底和 6 月初开始买入看跌期权，该比率于 6 月 24 日达到一年来的看跌高点，就在该基金达到顶峰并进入 25% 回撤的前两天。“今年夏天，银行对杠杆 ETF 的敞口和态势感知达到了这样的程度，他们感到非常容易面临半导体名称的跳跃风险，这导致对冲和波动性大幅上升，”芝加哥 Convexitas 首席信息官 Zed Francis 表示。该公司为客户运行半导体期权交易策略。 “现在他们不需要这些对冲，而且我相信这些对冲的解除已经使该行业的波动性变得便宜。” 让大资金逆势投资者排队吧。无论是半导体期权交易成本的下降——SMH隐含波动率周一从上个月的65%跌至40%，为2月份以来的最低水平——还是只是交易者想要淡出人群的冲动，有人在周一对该集团进行了大量押注。就在美国东部时间上午11点之前，根据 SpotGamma 和 ThinkOrSwim 的数据，纳斯达克 PHLX 交易所的交易员以 1.29 亿美元的价格买入了 20,100 手 630 次行使的 SMH 看跌期权，价格为 11 月 20 日到期。截至周五收盘，该合约的未平仓合约数量低于 50，这意味着该交易几乎肯定是一个新头寸。周一当时没有任何其他如此规模的交易，而且该基金的交易价格为 594 美元，深度实值看跌期权头寸很可能被用作对该集团的综合空头押注。根据 SpotGamma 的数据，这是周一盘中最大的单笔期权交易，比第二大交易（Sandisk 的多部分交易的 3700 万美元）大 3.5 倍。

“在这些半导体期权中，你走得越远，期权定价越愚蠢，人们就会押注价格上涨崩盘。”TheoTrade 联合创始人唐·考夫曼 (Don Kaufman) 表示。 “这本身就让我成为一个逆向投资者。”

title: “令人担忧”：欧洲央行经济学家警告称，人工智能正在推动迫在眉睫的市场调整
content:
美国随着投资者纷纷涌入人工智能热潮，欧洲股市正在创下历史新高，但欧洲央行的经济学家警告称，历史表明未来将出现急剧下滑。

经济学家在周一的博客中写道，“对过去技术革命的经济研究得出了一个令人担忧的结论：当前股市估值可能会出现修正”，并列举了两种潜在的情况。

可能会发生修正，因为“过度自信、过度乐观的投资者”将价格推高至超出其基本面水平他们表示，一旦繁荣消退，就会导致价格崩盘。

但他们补充道，即使目前的估值准确反映了人工智能重塑全球经济和提高企业利润的能力，价格下跌也是意料之中的。

经济学家们引用了与 19 世纪铁路繁荣、20 年代电力和广播的扩张以及 1990 年代互联网崛起的相似之处——这并不是第一次当前的人工智能浪潮与 2000 年代初期的互联网泡沫相比较。

在每种情况下，投资者对与技术相关的转型是否成功的紧张情绪都会蔓延到更广泛的经济领域。

“随着采用的蔓延……不确定性变得遍及整个经济。如果该技术出现问题，整个经济都会受到影响，”经济学家写道。

这促使投资者要求更高的风险溢价，他们的分析发现，这很可能最终会实现。即使利润增长依然强劲，也会导致股价下跌。

“这两种观点都意味着，在未来的某个时刻，繁荣之后会出现修正，或者从估值上涨的地方回调，”他们表示，并指出，这反过来可能会导致股市复苏和进一步攀升。

“具体时间无法提前得知。这些繁荣-萧条模式只能通过事后才能识别。”

该博客接着警告说，经济学家表示，由于全球指数基金和养老基金中盛行“Magnificent 7”股票，欧洲散户投资者的风险敞口很高，但可能在不知情的情况下。

还有进一步的风险，即急剧调整会通过基于基金的结构引发连锁反应，最终威胁欧元区的稳定。

“与互联网泡沫时期不同，今天的起点留给降息或使用财政政策缓冲影响的空间明显较小。”

title: 美国航空将增加座椅靠背屏幕和更大的头等舱以追赶达美航空和联合航空
content:
美国航空终于为座椅靠背屏幕开了绿灯，该公司正在努力缩小与竞争对手达美航空和联合航空的利润差距。但客户还需要等待一段时间。

配备 4K 显示屏的新屏幕将于 2028 年波音和空客交付的新飞机上开始出现。该航空公司还将对飞机进行改造，以便所有机舱的乘客都能够使用这些屏幕以及蓝牙音频配对和 USB-C 充电等其他附加功能。

几个月来，美国航空一直在“认真考虑”这项技术以及对机舱进行重大改造。该公司长期以来一直回避座椅靠背屏幕，高管们认为不值得为飞机增加设备成本和重量，并表示他们希望乘客使用自己的设备进行娱乐。

“自十多年前我们做出这一决定以来，这项技术已经进步了很多，”首席客户官希瑟·加博登(Heather Garboden)在接受采访时表示。 “最终，当你有了客户偏好和客户满意度提高时，也会产生收入。”

她拒绝透露美国航空在该计划上花费了多少，但表示安装应在 2030 年代初完成。

周二，美国航空宣布其改造将包括在空客 A321neos 和波音 737 Max 10 上安装更多头等舱座椅，尽管后者的交付还需要几年时间。美国航空还在其机队中增加更多腿部空间更大的座位。

这些高级座位的价格可能是经济舱票价的两倍或更多。例如，从纽约肯尼迪国际机场到达拉斯沃斯堡国际机场的往返机票，经济舱票价为 447 美元，头等舱票价为 1,161 美元。

美国航空公司首席执行官罗伯特·伊索姆 (Robert Isom) 6 月向 CNBC 表示，他和他的团队正在努力通过提供更多高级座位、豪华休息室和改善航空公司网络来缩小与大型航空公司竞争对手的利润差距。他表示，美国航空还计划用该公司的新商务舱套房翻新其波音 787-8 梦想飞机，并增加更多套房。该航空公司还在寻找新的宽体飞机市场，并一直在评估波音和空客的选择。

美国航空公布第二季度利润为 7100 万美元，而同期联合航空为 8.05 亿美元，达美航空为 16 亿美元。

title: 弗格森造船厂将裁员四分之一
content: Image source,Getty ImagesByCalum WatsonBBC ScotlandPublished18 August 2026, 09:24 BSTUpdated 5 hours agoScotland's state-owned shipyard is to cut nearly a quarter of its total workforce while it waits for confirmation of promised new orders.Workers at Ferguson Marine have been invited to apply for voluntary redundancy as construction draws to a close on the second of two long-delayed CalMac ferries.The Port Glasgow firm currently employs 247 core staff, 31 agency staff and 32 apprentices - but says it expects to shed 70 posts through a voluntary redundancy process.The Scottish government has promised to directly award the yard new orders for four smaller ships, but ministers say they are still conducting "due diligence" on the plan.Ferguson Marine said the job losses would protect the long-term viability of the yard - but unions described the move as "a betrayal of a blameless workforce".BBC Scotland News understands those who choose to leave the firm will receive Â£1,000 per completed year of service, up to Â£10,000, on top of their statutory entitlements.Image caption,The Ferguson shipyard faces a gap in orders despite promises of new work from the Scottish governmentFerguson Marine is the last commercial shipyard on the Clyde.It was nationalised in 2019 after a long dispute between its former owner and government-owned ferries agency Caledonian Maritime Assets Ltd (CMAL) over claims for extra costs for two dual-fuel CalMac ferries.The first, MV Glen Sannox, was finally delivered in November 2024, while MV Glen Rosa is due for completion by the end of this year.The shipyard recently completed sub-contracting work for BAE Systems for new Type 26 frigates and currently has no confirmed future orders.Ferguson Marine CEO Graeme Thomson said the yard's immediate focus was the handover of Glen Rosa before the end of this year."However, as the vessel nears completion, we face an inevitable gap in workload while we work with the Scottish government to make the relevant preparations to enable us to proceed with contract negotiations," he said."Shipbuilding capability relies on continuity and while changes of this nature are difficult, taking proactive action now ensures we protect the long-term viability of the yard and remain lean, modern, and ready to cut steel on the new fleet as quickly as possible."Image source,Ferguson MarineImage caption,The latest intake of 10 apprentices and their parents were recently given a tour of the yard before the trainees begin their first year in collegeIn March, before the Holyrood election, the Scottish government announced plans to directly award the shipyard contracts for four future vessels.It said the vessels - two small CalMac ferries, a fisheries research ship and a marine protection vessel - would provide a "bridge to the future" for the yard.The then Economy Secretary Kate Forbes said the government had "done a lot of the upfront work in terms of scoping out, securing some of the legal advice about what is possible".But she added that engagement with the Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) would be required.Since then none of the contracts have been confirmed, with ministers saying "due diligence" is still being carried out.BBC Scotland understands the Scottish government has not yet contacted the CMA for guidance on the legality of its proposals.Image source,Christopher BrindleImage caption,MV Glen Rosa has now been moved downriver to Inchgreen for final fitting out and commissioning, leaving the main Port Glasgow yard without a ship under construction for the first time in 12 yearsEconomy, Tourism and Transport Secretary Stephen Flynn said the redundancy scheme was part of efforts to modernise the shipyard and put it on a more competitive footing."The action that the leadership team at Ferguson Marine is taking today is necessary to help secure a viable future for the yard, and that of commercial shipbuilding on the Clyde," he said.Flynn said he had been assured that the reduced workforce would not affect the building of the MV Glen Rosa.And he added: "Our intention to directly award four vessels continues to undergo full due diligence further to next steps which will be announced to parliament in due course."'Shipbuilders need ships to build'Louise Gilmour, Scotland secretary of the GMB union, said ministers had failed to deliver new contracts while sending work around the world."Fergusons was once Scotland's ferry factory with a worldwide reputation for excellence and should be again," she said."Instead, skilled and experienced shipbuilders are being encouraged to leave as those in charge send contracts everywhere but here."She said the "hubris and incompetence" of those in charge of Scotland's ferry network had "failed a blameless workforce that deserves the chance to turn the page".On the delays in delivering the new contracts she commented: "Shipbuilders needs ships to build so where are those promised to Ferguson Marine? If they ever come, who will build them?"SNP backbencher Stuart MacMillan, who is the local MSP, said it was a "wake up call" for management but he also called on the Scottish government to speed up the promised new orders."My challenge to the Scottish government is to expedite the direct award process with the Competition and Markets Authority," he said.Local Labour MP Martin McCluskey said the news was "deeply concerning" and part of a "jobs crisis" in Inverclyde which has lost 1,500 jobs in recent years."The Scottish government needs to step up, move faster and do everything within its power to secure the future of Ferguson Marine and the skilled jobs that depend on it," he said.How can the Ferguson shipyard have a future?Published14 September 2025Why was Glen Sannox so hard to build?Published13 January 2025The Ferguson ships nobody talks aboutPublished26 November 2023Even if a new contract was awarded imminently, at least a year of design work would be required before the yard would be in a position to start cutting steel.While the promised new orders have yet to be confirmed, they have allowed the firm to update its business plan, potentially unlocking theÂ£14.2m of modernisation money first announced by ministers more than two years ago.Ground investigation work is taking place with a view to installing new equipment and software which is hoped to raise productivity.The shipyard's apprentice programme is also unaffected by the redundancies in the short term, with 34 young workers already in training and a new intake of 10 trainees about to start their first year in college.Why is the shipyard struggling for orders?Ferguson's has successfully built more than 360 ships since it was founded by four brothers in 1903, but its reputation has been harmed by the controversy over the long-delayed and over-budget ferries MV Glen Sannox and MV Glen Rosa.Construction of the first liquefied natural gas (LNG) vessels of their kind ever built in the UK was blighted by design challenges and disputes over claims for extra costs.While there is wide agreement the workforce were not to blame, the controversy may have left potential customers nervous about placing new orders.The shipyard also faces wider challenges, in common with all UK shipbuilders, of having to compete on cost with overseas firms, particularly in eastern Europe and the Far East.The Society of Maritime Industries says foreign yards are typically able to undercut UK-based shipbuilders by 10-20% due to a mix of cheaper labour and better state support.Image source,Ferguson archiveImage caption,The Ferguson shipyard has built more than 360 ships since its first vessel, a tug called Flying Swift, took to the water in 1903Two years ago Ferguson'smissed out on an order for seven small CalMac shipswhich was widely regarded as an ideal contract to help rebuild the firm's reputation.While its bid was praised for its quality, CMAL awarded the deal to a Polish firm because it could build the ships more cheaply.Ferguson's management has repeatedly called for "social value" to be factored into such evaluations, which would recognise the wider economic benefits of building ships in Scotland rather than focusing on the headline price.But CMALclaims it is restricted in its ability to score bids for social valuebecause Scotland's pre-Brexit procurement rules mean it must treat all bidders equally.Last summer Ferguson's boss Graeme Thomsoncalled for the direct award of another CalMac ship, a replacement for MV Lord of the Isles.He described it as a "target contract" and warned it would be "very difficult" to sustain workforce numbers if the yard did not secure the work.But his appeal was rejected by ministers, and the contract went out to tender earlier this year.Ferguson's was unable to bid for the work because CMAL set pre-qualification criteria which, according to Ferguson's management,no UK-based commercial shipbuilder was capable of fulfillingA shortlist of bidders has now been drawn up, but CMAL has declined to reveal which firms are on it or where they are based, on grounds that this would harm competition. The winning bidder will be announced early next year.Related topicsPort GlasgowFerries

title: 英伟达的AI护城河正在从芯片转向资本
content:
Nvidia'smassive head start in artificial intelligence turned the chipmaker into the world's most valuable company. Now, almost four years into the generative AI boom, competitors likeAdvanced Micro DevicesandGooglehave chipped away at Nvidia's technology lead, pushing the company to take advantage of its other great asset: capital.

Following last week'spactwith Wall Street firms to pursue $500 billion worth of financing for Nvidia's graphics processing units, Nvidiasaidon Monday that it's providing up to $105 billion for a giant OpenAI data center in Ohio, offering a backstop of sorts should the ChatGPT creator see its fortunes turn.

For Nvidia, the strategy involves fueling the AI boom by whatever means necessary, recognizing that demand for critical infrastructure is seemingly insatiable but that a handful of companies — the hyperscalers — account for an outsized amount of purchases. With its quarterly free cash flow up 18-fold over the past three years to $48.5 billion in thelatest period, Nvidia is using the strength of its balance sheet and credit rating to ensure there's no dramatic slowdown following 12 straight quarters of revenue growth above 55%.

"They remain dominant, but they're very paranoid about making sure they don't lose ground," said Ram Bala, associate professor of AI and analytics at Santa Clara University's Leavey School of Business.

In a note to clients on Monday, analysts at Cantor brushed off concerns that Nvidia is effectively buying revenue through its financial maneuvering. They reiterated their buy rating and said the latest agreement is a "clear signal that the current AI investment cycle will be elongated and durable."

"We view this less as circular and more facilitating the coming AI buildout while at the same time creating additional competitive moats that will continue to enable NVDA to remain THE AI leader," the analysts wrote.

Nvidia is swimming in money. Its cash generation is so great that the companysaidin May that it was increasing its quarterly dividend to 25 cents a share from a penny, and announced a new $80 billion stock buyback plan. The company pledged "to return roughly 50% of free cash flow to shareholders this year."

One way the company has been putting its cash pile to work is through equity investments in companies across the AI ecosystem, including some businesses — like model developers and neoclouds — that spend heavily on Nvidia's chips and systems. Nvidia held $30.2 billion in marketable equity securities as of the most recent quarter, up from $12.9 billion a year earlier.

In February, Nvidiainvested $30 billionin OpenAI, which relies on training capacity from Vera Rubin, the chip giant's most advanced system. Monday's agreement included a $1.5 billion investment in SB Energy, a SoftBank affiliate that's building and managing the data center at the PORTS-Pike Technology Campus in Pike County, Ohio, through a 20-year lease to OpenAI.

In addition to the SB Energy investment, Nvidia said it's putting its financial support behind about 4 gigawatts of development at the Ohio site for portions of lease and power and "a specified residual-value commitment," as data centers open between 2028 and 2030.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang acknowledged the significance of the company's financial prowess in apost on Xabout the agreement.

"Frontier AI labs have extraordinary demand for training and inference compute, but many are growing faster than their balance sheets and long-term credit profiles can support," Huang wrote. "They may have strong customer demand and rapidly growing revenue yet still lack the decades-long infrastructure contracts and investment-grade financing capacity needed to secure the AI factory infrastructure independently."

A week prior, Huang was on set at CNBC surrounded by six of Wall Street's leading financiers to announce the arrival of Nvidia graphics processing units as a new asset class. In signing a memorandum of understanding with firms includingGoldman Sachs,Apollo Global Management,Blackstone andBlackRock, Huang indicated that the next phase of the AI buildout will be funded in part by third-party backers, who can start investing in GPUs the way they do real estate.

"These are revenue-generating assets now," Huang told CNBC. "They're productive, they're long-lived, they're fungible, they're flexible."

Key to obtaining financing for prospective borrowers will be a dedication to Huang's systems, with Nvidia obtaining the option of backstopping 25% of every loan. It's another way to get more of Nvidia's technology into the market, as competition builds from Google and AMD, as well as from specialized chipmakers likeCerebras.

In the second quarter, Google began recognizing revenue from TPU system sales, contributing to the cloud unit's82% growth. AMD, meanwhile,reportedmore than 100% growth in its data center business, and the company expects its first rack-scale system, called Helios, to ship later this year.

Paul Meeks, head of technology research at Freedom Capital Markets, said the stepped-up competition eats into Nvidia's ability to yield "outrageous margins," and incentives the company to diversify its strategy.

"Part of their thinking is let's broaden our reach," Meeks said. "We just can't ride this one horse, which is GPUs."

AI bulls say that Nvidia is just responding to demand, and point out that the shortage in the market today is on the capacity side. There are plenty of numbers to back that up, asAnthropictold investorsover the weekend that its annualized revenue run rate hit $65 billion in July, up sevenfold from a year earlier.OpenAI'srun rate recently reached $40 billion.

Matthew Vegari, head of research at Clearwater Analytics, said in an email that, based on the market dynamics, the "narrative around the AI trade's circuitous, 'house of cards' structure strikes us as somewhat misguided."

"We might one day be at overcapacity," he wrote. "But that day isn't today."

— CNBC's Samantha Subin and Jonathan Vanian contributed to this report

title: 这家初创公司利用人工智能帮助罕见疾病家庭开发定制治疗方法
content:
CNBC Cures is proudly underwritten by Alexion, AstraZeneca Rare Disease, whose support enables our journalism to elevate stories that advance research, innovation and patient care in rare diseases.

Jacalyn Lee first sensed something was off with her daughter, Isla, just before her first birthday.

"She was just under a year old, and nobody believed me, including the pediatrician," she said.

Isla was missing some of the developmental milestones that her sisters had hit at her age. Doctors told Lee that her two other daughters were just advanced, and that she should not be measuring Isla's development against theirs.

But by the time Isla was 15 months, Jacalyn had grown more insistent.

"I said to my husband, because I couldn't go to the pediatrician appointment, 'You do not leave that pediatrician appointment without getting some type of referral for an eval. Something is different, I'm telling you.'"

A few months later, Isla was diagnosed with autism. It wasn't until her parents received the results of a genetic test when Isla was 3 years old that they realized the cause of her struggles. Isla was diagnosed with DEAF1-Associated Neurodevelopmental Disorder, or DAND — an ultra-rare group of genetic conditions characterized by developmental delays, intellectual disability, and autism. Only about 200 patients have been diagnosed with the disease worldwide.

"We were handed this diagnosis, and little else. There was no roadmap, barely any research, no community that I was aware of at the time," Jacalyn said.

Lee, who works as a communications strategist, said she channeled her grief into action — gathering all the information she could about DAND while connecting with researchers and other parents of children with the same condition. She and four other mothers launchedThe DAND Alliance, a group that was able to raise money towards developing a treatment. But figuring out what to do next became more difficult.

For the five working moms, life had already become an unsustainable series of meetings with researchers. Lee said the group needed to find a partner who understood the work that they were doing, and knew how to help move the project forward.

"We were trying to figure out where should we spend money, knowing that we only have so much. But really we wanted this final document that was board-ready, that we could use to fundraise against, that we could use to operationalize against… almost like a pipeline with sequencing of, okay, you need A to get to B to get to C," Lee said. "We still needed to kind of untangle and create a path forward that was easy to understand, easy to digest in terms of what we needed to focus on right now."

The group turned to Nome for help, a startup trying to position itself as a contract research organization, or CRO, dedicated to serving smaller rare disease groups that the pharma industry does not often cater too.

"We act with patient-level urgency and are highly focused on providing a roadmap forward for an underserved part of the market," said Stevie Ringel, Nome's founder and CEO.

In the case of DAND Alliance, Nome provided the group with a 53-page report detailing next steps and outlining everything from animal studies to trial design.

"They helped us figure out what the gaps are, what work streams we need to prioritize, and even potential researchers or vendors that we need to think about engaging with," Lee said.

Lee said Ringel delivered it all within a timeframe, and at a price point, that surprised her.

"I think he got it in terms of the speed in which we wanted to move and how urgent this was for us, the fact that we were so new, we didn't have a lot of funding," Lee said.

Ringel understood the sense of urgency for Isla because, in many ways, her journey mirrors that of his own.

As a teenager, Ringel and his sister were both diagnosed with a type of retinal dystrophy caused by a mutation of the KIZ gene — a rare inherited genetic eye disorder that impacts less than 200 patients globally. There are no FDA-approved treatment options.

Ringel launched theKizuna Foundation, and was able to raise money towards developing an individualized treatment, but the work required to get there, coupled with a lack of certainty around the process, was taxing.

Ringel designed Nome with that in mind. He said he built the company to be exactly what his own foundation needed — a service for small patient groups looking to develop personalized treatments. One that provides guidance after funds are raised, but before significant capital is deployed.

"As a patient, it would have made a world of difference to me to hear, you know, actually there's something we can do. It's gonna be long and hard and potentially expensive, but there's a pathway here that's credible, here's what it is, and here's how you can take action — versus, sorry, go learn Braille," Ringel said.

That's what inspired Ringel to launch Nome, which he calls a "white glove service" for developing treatments for underserved patient populations.

"People come to us one family at a time, or as a collection of families."

The goal is to bring down the cost of individualized therapies and to make them more attainable for smaller patient groups — maybe even one day providing a path for insurance to pay for them.

Here's how it works. After a patient receives a genetic test that identifies a genetic disorder, they can upload the test results into Nome's system. Nome uses an AI platform that it built — one that it says is more accurate than readily available consumer models — to search for potential treatment options. Nome then provides a free detailed report on the findings.

Ringel sees Nome as providing insight after a diagnostic test. He wants to work in tandem with clinicians and genetic counselors — identifying pathways toward a treatment shortly after a genetic disorder is identified.

"We've built an AI system that can do that analysis in about 10 minutes. And we have a PhD in the loop on top of that before we send anything back to a patient. But it really allows us to give back that answer in a few minutes versus dozens of hours."

Ringel said Nome currently does between 80 and 100 of these reports per month. Of the roughly 5,000 cases Nome has looked at to date, Ringel said the company has identified a programmable medicine or an existing custom medical therapy that fits the known mutation about 25% of the time.

Nome makes money when customers hire them to help design clinical trials for those treatment options, or to act as a project manager to usher the drug to a point where it can be built and delivered to the patients that need them.

"Once we tell you that it's possible, you contract with us to do all the actual hard work and heavy lifting, like a concierge drug developer working for you," Ringel said. "We don't want to send people off into the wilderness. We want them to say, 'no, please help me take this all the way through to dosing.'"

Nome, which oversees a little more than 10 genetic medicine programs, uses AI models to help design trials and manage logistics of those program operations. Ringel said about 25% of the work done at Nome is automated using its AI systems. He believes that as the company's AI agents train and get more advanced over the next one to two years, Nome can automate 60%-80% of the process.

In personalized medicine, where human capital can account for so much of a drug's development costs, Ringel believes a better use of AI will be key in making these kinds of treatments more accessible.

"We know that a customized ASO is between $1.2 and $1.4 million," Ringel said. "If we can bring the cost down by 50%, we hope we can create a pathway where insurance might even start to pay for them."

He compared it to CAR-T cancer therapies. Once seen astoo expensivefor insurance to pay for, approved CAR-T therapies are now covered by most public and private insurance plans.

Ringel acknowledges that Nome is very early to all of this, and that there's still a long way to go before the company is able to fully accomplish what he envisions for it. To skeptics, who say Nome provides an added layer of cost to an already expensive process, Ringel says he's just trying to provide a service to patient groups who desperately need it.

"I don't know how you can expect these families to move this process forward without someone playing quarterback," Ringel said. "We think we'll ultimately save these groups money, and we'll save them time."

He considers Nome a logistics play. "We call it drug development operations," he said. "We're just trying to connect great science to the people that need it."

When it comes to the science, Nome turns to the more than 80 partners that it works with — groups like La Jolla Labs and Dyno Therapeutics — who have expertise in drug development.

For Jacalyn Lee, the promise of scientific development is what initially gave her hope following Isla's diagnosis.

"I really believe that we are in this renaissance era of AI and gene therapy and patient advocacy," Lee said.

"A nurse at the doctor's office told us, 'the slow curve of progress is now a vertical line.' So I really try to hold onto that."

And Lee hopes Nome could potentially offer a shorter path towards the progress that she desperately clings to.

"In a really acute time, where you just get this devastating diagnosis, and there's no roadmap, there's no cure that you know of, and there's barely any research out there, it's very isolating. And so, if you can have a service

title: 俄罗斯称其经济强劲。它刚刚解雇了一位发出相反警告的顶级经济学家
content:
俄罗斯政府官员向 CNBC 表示，尽管自 2022 年初全面入侵乌克兰以来，尽管面临“前所未有的外国压力”，但俄罗斯经济仍然强劲且健康。

这一信息与俄罗斯国家控制的开发银行 VEB 前首席经济学家的观点形成鲜明对比。后者在今年早些时候发表的言论被用俄语报道后于周日被解雇。媒体。

据报道，前经济副部长安德烈·克莱帕奇 (Andrei Klepach) 在提交一份报告后被解雇，该报告警告俄罗斯无法赢得与乌克兰的长期消耗战，并预测将出现重大社会危机。

据流亡的俄罗斯独立媒体《贝尔》报道，克莱帕奇的被解雇与其严厉的经济评估直接相关，该报在首次报道这一消息时援引了熟悉此事的未透露姓名的消息来源。 CNBC 无法独立核实该报道。

根据翻译，Klepach 在 5 月 21 日向经济学家同事发表的演讲中表示，“在这场消耗战中，我们不会赢得竞争。我们幻想一切都会崩溃。事实并非如此，也不会。我们的成本正在不断增加。”

“我相信俄罗斯不会崩溃，但我几乎可以肯定我们最终会陷入社会危机。我们经济上不会崩溃，但我们的滞后将会扩大，并带来随之而来的所有后果。”他补充道。

解雇克莱帕奇的举动似乎突显了克里姆林宫在近四年半的战争之后对公众批评和反对其在乌克兰的军事行动采取的零容忍态度。

俄罗斯政府官员仍然对该国的经济状况表现出挑衅态度。

俄罗斯驻乌克兰大使馆英国向 CNBC 表示，俄罗斯的财政状况仍然“明显强于”许多西方经济体，并指出其外国公共债务约为 570 亿美元，并指出这“大大低于”美国、英国、意大利或法国仅用于偿债的金额。

“俄罗斯经济保持弹性，我们人民的意愿也是如此，”俄罗斯驻英国大使馆发言人告诉 CNBC

“通过经济压力削弱俄罗斯的企图并没有产生作者预期的结果，”他们补充道。

“相反，包括英国在内的西方国家本身正在为其鲁莽的制裁政策付出巨大代价。英国企业失去了进入俄罗斯市场的机会，而供应链中断以及能源和大宗商品成本上涨给英国经济带来了额外成本。

安德斯·阿斯伦德（Anders Aslund），瑞典经济学家、前高级研究员。大西洋理事会表示，克莱帕奇被解职的消息并不令人意外。

阿斯伦德周日通过 X 表示：“在一项著名分析中，他得出的结论是，俄罗斯无法赢得对乌克兰的消耗战，俄罗斯很可能最终陷入 1917 年那样的社会危机。”

另外，国际战略研究所俄罗斯和欧亚地区高级研究员奈杰尔·古尔德-戴维斯研究称克莱帕奇非常有能力和聪明。

“我早就说过，俄罗斯最优秀的经济头脑是最惊慌的。这再次证实了这一点。”古尔德-戴维斯周一通过社交媒体表示。

最近几周，乌克兰对炼油厂和交货仓库进行远程无人机袭击，俄罗斯的战时经济成为人们更加关注的焦点。

尽管最近的数据显示，俄罗斯战时经济的增长超出预期，甚至增长缓慢，但分析人士表示，这掩盖了一些问题，例如克里姆林宫对军费开支、更高税收和补贴银行的依赖等。贷款。

title: Wetherspoons 禁止顾客在酒吧里用手机播放音乐
content: 图片来源，Mike Kemp/In Pictures via Getty Images 作者：Mitchell Labiak 商业记者 6 分钟前发布 Wetherspoons 禁止其顾客大声播放音乐或通过扬声器接听电话，称噪音是一个日益严重的问题，让人们“发疯”。该公司在英国经营着 792 家酒馆和酒吧，表示收到投诉后，已要求顾客将手机和平板电脑调至静音或使用近年来，各种组织的民意调查表明，人们在很大程度上反对其他人在公共场所播放音乐或通过扬声器接听电话。Wetherspoons 告诉 BBC，在执行禁令时，工作人员将被要求运用“常识”。该公司表示，“我们不会要求任何人在违反裁决的情况下离开酒吧，但如果他们拒绝这样做，经理们可以选择这样做。”除了禁止说脏话外，还禁止使用电话或任何形式的科技产品。Wetherspoons 不在其任何酒吧内播放音乐，首席执行官蒂姆·马丁 (Tim Martin) 将其描述为“宁静和沉思的绿洲”。该连锁店在其 44 家 Lloyds' 酒吧晚上确实会播放音乐。它确认，禁止顾客播放音乐和通过扬声器接听电话的禁令也适用于这些场所。Wetherspoons 酒吧的数量从 2015 年末的 955 家峰值开始，在过去十年中稳步下降。在这十年里，该公司面临着新冠疫情和通货膨胀带来的财务挑战。上个月，该公司告诉投资者，由于食品、劳动力、维修、能源和营业税成本上升，今年的利润将低于预期。主题公司 Wetherspoons 酒店业酒吧更多关于这个故事的内容为什么扬声器上的电话可能会成为另一种噪音发布于 8 月 6 日第一所大学拥有的 Wetherspoons 将于 5 月开业发布发布于 2 月 18 日

title: 人工智能帮助飞机避免气候变暖的“天空涂鸦”
content: Image source,Getty ImagesImage caption,Contrails are formed when exhaust fumes from planes turn into ice crystalsByShiona McCallumSenior technology reporterPublished4 hours agoWe've all looked up and seen the white lines trailing behind aircraft in the sky.Known as contrails, these icy clouds contribute to climate change, and scientists have been trying to work out how to stop them.Now, a Â£5m UK trial will test whether AI can help, by predicting where warming contrails are likely to form and getting planes to avoid those areas.It will focus on the Shanwick Oceanic airspace in the eastern half of the North Atlantic corridor which accounts for approximately 5% of global contrail warming.The 30-month Operation Blue Skies project brings together Google, the UK government, the Met Office, air traffic control provider National Air Traffic Services (NATS) and researchers at the University of Cambridge and Imperial College London.Contrails - also known as vapour trails - are made when the hot exhaust from aircraft engines meets the cold air at high altitude, creating ice crystals.Many disappear quickly, but in particularly cold and humid conditions they can persist and spread, forming clouds which trap heat that would otherwise escape from the Earth.Dr Paul Hodgson, Google's technical lead for the operation, told the BBC's Tech Life programme his five-year-old has a more colourful description for the white lines - "sky graffiti"."We think that contrail warming is responsible for something like a third of all aviation climate warming," he said.Dr Hodgson acknowledged there was uncertainty around the precise figure, but said scientists were confident it was "either quite a large problem or a very large problem".The project also comes as the government backs expansion of UK airports, raising the wider question of whether tech solutions can sufficiently reduce aviation's environmental impact as demand for flying grows.Google is also one of many big tech companies spending billions onnew data centres- the giant, power-hungry banks of computer chips which power AI - which environmentalists are concerned will contribute even more to climate change.Image source,Getty ImagesImage caption,Contrails - or condensation trails - are a regular feature in our skiesThe idea behind the trial is that if scientists can predict the areas of the atmosphere where contrails are likely to form, aircraft could avoid them.Google will use satellite images and flight data to identify where planes have previously produced contrails.This is then combined with weather patterns to forecast where the conditions for new contrails are likely to occur.The information will be passed to NATS, where air traffic controllers can direct pilots to avoid those areas.Rather than dramatically changing the route of a flight, the trial will mostly involve changing an aircraft's altitude by around 2,000ft.This is something which already happens routinely to avoid turbulence and bad weather so passengers are unlikely to notice.Ian Jopson, director of sustainability at NATS, said it should be "pretty much business as usual using existing procedures for the operators on the North Atlantic".Testing will take place during selected evenings and nights in the winters of 2026-27 and 2027-28, when air traffic is lower.Around 10,000 flights are expected to pass through the airspace during the trial periods, although only a fraction will need to change altitude specifically to avoid contrails.The Department for Transport is providing Â£2.65m towards the programme, while Google is contributing Â£1.4m through AI research, engineering and computing infrastructure.A net climate benefit?Aviation Minister Keir Mather said the project would test "small tweaks to flight paths over the Atlantic" which could help make flying cleaner."This is a world-first, and it's British ingenuity leading the way," he said.Changing the altitude of an aircraft can mean it burns more fuel, raising an obvious question - could avoiding contrails simply create additional carbon emissions elsewhere?Hodgson said previous trials suggested the additional fuel use was much smaller than the climate benefit of preventing a warming contrail."The CO2 penalty is in the order of less than 1%, compared to the contrail cost, which is of a similar order magnitude to all of the CO2 of aviation," he said.Modelling for Operation Blue Skies suggests a full deviation through Shanwick would mean around 100kg of additional fuel per affected aircraft.Previous airline-level trials have achieved reductions of around 60-70% in contrail formation or warming, according to Hodgson.The results of Operation Blue Skies are expected to be published in academic literature and opened to wider scientific scrutiny.The truth behind the chemtrails conspiracy theoryPublished23 July 2022Reducing plane clouds can help climate - studyPublished24 September 2024How adjusting flight plans can help the climatePublished22 October 2021Sign up for our Tech Decoded newsletterto follow the world's top tech stories and trends.Outside the UK? title: 尽管英超俱乐部亏损飙升，投资者如何从足球中获利
content:
芬威体育集团周五将利物浦足球俱乐部的少数股权出售给包括杰夫·贝佐森在内的财团，交易价值超过 70 亿美元。

在这家总部位于波士顿的集团以 3 亿英镑（4.059 亿美元）的低价将利物浦从管理边缘拯救出来近 16 年后，FSG 在经历了一场令人瞩目的转变后，以巨额投资回报部分兑现了默西塞德俱乐部赢得了多项冠军国内和欧洲奖杯。

尽管英格兰足球俱乐部越来越吸引全球成熟投资者的兴趣，但它们仍然存在风险，而且往往无利可图。

德勤的年度足球财务审查发现，20个英超俱乐部在2024/25赛季的税前损失总计达9.48亿英镑，比上一赛季“显着恶化”超过600%

根据德勤的数据，当年只有 8 家具乐部报告了营业利润，而上一赛季有 13 家具乐部。

球员转会费虚高是运营成本高昂的一个关键因素。

“随着球员转会支出不断增长，以跟上不断升级的人才争夺战，今年很可能又将是出现巨额财务损失的一年，”德勤研究人员写道。

但是。

但是FSG 与利物浦的交易表明了购买被低估的资产并随后以更高价格出售的机会，随着人们对游戏的兴趣日益浓厚，推动球队估值越来越高。

“即使你没有日复一日地盈利，资产的价值仍在上涨，而且其中有大量资产可以被授权出去，”Brand Finance 全球董事总经理 Richard Haigh 在 CNBC 的“Squawk Box Europe”节目中表示。周一。

这取决于精英俱乐部可以提供的声誉和稀缺性，黑格说。

“英超联赛确实有助于英国的软实力，”他补充道。 “它是体育界最古老的联赛之一，具有全球影响力，在提高赞助商的商业价值方面利润非常丰厚。”

俱乐部越来越多地优化其现有的收入来源，例如比赛日门票收入。

“美国体育界做得非常好的另一件事，投资者希望在欧洲做的是，体育场和周围的房地产是一个 24/7、365 天的收入来源，而不是 24/7、365 天的收入来源。 Goodwin 合伙人兼体育金融专家 Lewis Gaut 表示：“这比每两周才赚钱一次的地方更好。”

UBS 在 6 月份写道，托特纳姆热刺足球俱乐部的新体育场建于 2019 年，耗资 12 亿英镑，其商业收入从 2018 年的 1.17 亿英镑跃升至 2022 年的 2.15 亿英镑。

2026 年，该体育场举办了大型音乐表演。包括 Gorillaz、Bad Bunny 和韩国流行音乐巨头 BTS。它也是美国以外第一座专门建造的 NFL 体育场，每年至少举办两场比赛。

高特补充道：“体育村可以在一个目的地举办多种体育运动和其他活动，有助于确保随时产生收入。”

曼联已确认计划建造一座新的 100,000 个座位的体育场，作为当地码头周围更广泛的重建项目的一部分。估计成本约为 20 亿英镑。

瑞银表示，这些雄心勃勃的体育场项目的目标反映了“对足球俱乐部在经济上所代表的含义进行更广泛的重新评估：具有多元化现金流的稀缺资产，而不是纯粹的体育或文化项目。”

虽然基础设施投资的收益可能需要几年时间才能实现，但投资者更专注于扩大和推动独立收入流。

“购买这些特许经营权的人知道体育资产是体育投资机构 Pinto Capital 合伙人 Amber Pinto 周五对 CNBC 的“Squawk Box Europe”节目表示：“成本当然很重要，但在考虑为什么有人要投资或购买当今排名前十的体育特许经营权时，成本并不是全部。”

title: 受油价上涨和收益率上升的影响，华尔街本周开局下跌，股票期货几乎没有变化：实时更新
content:
U.S. stock futures fell early Tuesday after the major averages began the new week on a losing note, as tensions between the U.S. and Iran persisted and inflation concerns led to higher Treasury yields.

Dow Jones Industrial Average futurestraded 73 points lower.S&P 500 futuresfell 0.32% along withNasdaq-100 futures, which were down 0.59%.

In Asia, South Korea's benchmarkKospijumped 1.9% Tuesday, while Japan'sNikkei 225fell 0.94%. Australia'sS&P/ASX 200edged 0.19% higher. Hong Kong'sHang Seng Indexslid 0.19%, while the CSI 300 lost 0.12%.

The moves in U.S. futures follow a losing session for stocks, as oil prices climbed more than 2% on uncertainty around a U.S.-Iran ceasefire that expired Monday. Negotiations between the countries have stalled, and President Donald Trump said he wouldattack Oman"if it gets in the way."

The rise in oil prices stoked inflation fears, driving longer-dated Treasury yields higher. The30-year Treasury bond yieldreached a peak not seen since June 2007.

Leading the way lower for stocks were the Dow and S&P 500, with each benchmark losing 0.5%. The Nasdaq was a relative outperformer, though it still pulled back by 0.3%.

Sonali Basak, chief investment strategist at iCapital, still thinks there's fuel left in the stock market, however, especially as the rally broadens beyond Big Tech.

"You look around and there's still more room to run," Basak told CNBC's "Closing Bell" in an interview. "Even in the last month, the S&P Equal Weight still did not outperform the Nasdaq or the SOXX — which tells me it's still been relatively left behind, even in recent days."

On the economic data front, investors will pore over import and export pricing figures for July, along with housing starts and pending home sales.Home Depotwill also post second-quarter earnings before the bell.

U.S. Treasury yields pushed higher Tuesday, with longer-dated yields remaining near multi-decade highs as investors continued to sell government bonds.

The30-year Treasury yieldrose about 1 basis point to 5.32%, around its highest level since 2007, while the20-year yieldclimbed to 5.316%. The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield added roughly 1.2 basis points to 4.736%.

Concerns over the U.S. fiscal outlook and heavy debt supply have added to pressure from elevated oil prices and renewed geopolitical tensions, sending yields higher.

"Long-term yields look likely to push up to 5.60-5.70% and likely move up at a quicker pace than normal," said Fundstrat's technical strategist Mark Newton.

He also pointed to Japan, where weaker-than-expected economic growth was accompanied by a hotter-than-expected GDP deflator. Japanese government bond yields rose following the data, with the move spilling into U.S. Treasurys and lifted yields on longer-duration debt.

Oil rose Tuesday amid concerns over supply disruptions and a potential resumption of Mideast hostilities after PresidentDonald Trumpsaid he would not extend the Iran ceasefire.

Futures for international benchmarkBrent crudefor October delivery gained 0.48% at $91.31 a barrel. U.S.West Texas Intermediate futuresfor September advanced 0.62% at $85.02per barrel.

Trumpalso said on Monday said the U.S. would "bomb the s--- out of" Oman if the Gulf nation "gets in the way," raising worries over growing strains in the Middle East.

"Crude prices are rising on renewed geopolitical tensions triggered by President Trump threatening Oman with military strikes and communicating that he is in no rush to end the Iran war," said José Torres, a senior economist at Interactive Brokers.

Mideast hostilities may also escalate following "a fresh burst of violence in Lebanon [that] is worrying market participants, Torres added.

The Japanese yenhovered around 159 against the dollar on Tuesday, having given back a significant portion of the gains sparked by last month's coordinated U.S.-Japan intervention.

In a note on Tuesday, Macquarie estimated U.S. authorities sold about $500 million worth of euros for yen on July 31, a fraction of the roughly $85 billion it estimates Japan spent buying yen with dollars over July 30 and 31.

That suggests the impact of Washington's involvement came primarily from the signal it sent to markets rather than the size of its intervention, according to Gareth Berry, Macquarie's head of FX and rates strategy.

Still, Berry said the relatively small U.S. operation means Washington has substantial capacity to step in again if the yen weakens further. Macquarie estimates the U.S. Treasury and Federal Reserve have another $25.9 billion in euro-denominated reserves that could be deployed through EUR/JPY, allowing them to repeat interventions of a similar size many times.

If authorities instead intervene directly in USD/JPY, Macquarie said the available firepower could, in theory, be "almost limitless."

The gap between the Chinese 10-year government bond yield and U.S.10-year Treasuryis widening again, reflecting growing divergence between the world's two largest economies.

The spread climbed to 303 basis points Monday, matching levels seen on July 31, and headed toward a high of 315 basis points seen in January 2025, according to Wind Information data going back to 2007.

As China's economy has struggled with weak domestic demand, the 10-year government bond yield has persistently traded below that of the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield since 2022.

Weaker-than-expected China economic data released Monday raised expectations ofpolicy easing, which if followed through increase the yield spread further.

In theU.S., Treasury yields rose, with the30-yearhitting its highest since June 2007, as rising oil prices added to investor worries about high inflation and government debt levels.

— CNBC's Sean Conlon and Hugh Leask contributed to this report.

Asia-Pacific markets traded largely lower Tuesday, with South Korean stocks bucking the broader decline after resuming trade from a holiday.

South Korea's benchmarkKospijumped 2%, powered by gains in chip giants Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix which added 3% and 5% respectively.

Japan'sNikkei 225was down 0.9% while the Topix declined 0.28%.

Australia's benchmarkS&P/ASX 200was flat at the open.

Asia-Pacific markets were set to fall Tuesday asU.S. President Donald Trumpruled out extending a 60-day agreement with Iran that had led to a fragile ceasefire between the two countries, while also threatening Oman with military action.

Japan'sNikkei 225Chicago futures contract was trading at 68,990 and its Osaka counterpart was last at 68,970 compared with the index's previous close of 69,220.25.

Hong Kong'sHang Seng indexfutures last traded at 25,355, below the benchmark's close of 25,453.23.

Futures for Australia'sS&P/ASX 200last traded at 8,976 compared with the index's last close of 9,073.2.

Trump said informal talks were underway with Iran's Revolutionary Guard but that he was "not in a hurry" to reach an agreement. "They're good poker players, but they're dying," he told Fox News.

Hours later, Trump said he would not seek to extend the temporary truce. "No," he told reporters when asked about an extension.

Shares fell over 4.5% in regular trading for the defense contracting giantL3Harris Technologiesafter the company removed CEO Chris Kubasik.

The company ousted Kubasik after discovering he engaged "certain conduct ... that was not consistent with the values of the Company," L3Harris Technologies said in a statement Monday. Kubasik has been replaced bySam Mehtaas chief executive officer and president.

After Monday's close, shares were up marginally.

Dow Jones Industrial Average futurestraded 32 points lower.S&P 500 futuresfell marginally along withNasdaq-100 futures.

title: 李总统表示，随着特朗普削减军事演习，韩国必须为“最坏情况”做好准备
content:
韩国总统李在明周二表示，维持和平对国家来说“最重要”，但需要为“最坏的情况”做好准备。他发表此番言论之前，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普命令国防部长皮特·赫格斯“大幅减少”与首尔的联合演习，以免向朝鲜“发出完全不恰当和敌对的信号”。与朝鲜领导人金正恩的关系“非常好”，并形容该国“没有威胁性且相互尊重”。

据 CNBC 翻译的韩国新闻稿称，李周二表示，名为“乙支自由之盾”的年度演习是防御性的，无意攻击朝鲜或加剧半岛紧张局势。

周一开始的联合军事演习计划持续到 8 月 27 日，约有 18,000 名韩国人参加军事人员参加。

平壤长期以来一直谴责联合演习，称其为入侵朝鲜的预演。

该国外交部上周在一份声明中表示，“（美国）这样做，并没有隐瞒其为与朝鲜进行实质性军事对抗做好准备的目的。

“这等于承认美国和朝鲜进行的演习。韩国将其描述为‘年度’和‘防御性’战争，是一场侵略战争的预演，”它补充道。

特朗普发表此番言论的同时，他还指责首尔在与伊朗的冲突中没有帮助美国，他周一表示，“我们有 39,000 名士兵在那里保护你们免受邻国金正恩的伤害，你们不会帮助我们在朝鲜进行一场非常简单的军事行动。”伊朗。”

美国韩国军队是华盛顿驻韩部队的指挥机构，由约 28,500 名人员组成。

韩国总统办公室官员表示，“我们正在与美方密切讨论实际和军事贡献措施，同时考虑到朝鲜半岛的准备情况和国内法律程序等各种因素，”韩国媒体周一报道。

特朗普利用围绕演习的言论和时机，试图战略与国际研究中心韩国主席 Victor Cha 表示，吸引朝鲜金正恩与他会面。

Cha 在 CSIS 的播客中补充道，“这并不是什么不寻常的事情。我们过去曾看到总统使用军事演习作为工具。”

早在 2018 年，特朗普就因平壤和华盛顿之间正在进行谈判而暂停了与韩国的演习。

Cha 还表示我们现在看到这种情况的部分原因是，对特朗普来说，演习的时机是发出具体信息并获得有关伊朗的头条新闻的有用工具。

“特朗普厌倦了伊朗……所以他正在转向其他事情。”

——CNBC 的 Jenny Lee 对本报告作出了贡献。

title: 美伊停火到期可能引发长期冲突，霍尔木兹海峡发生船只袭击
content:
英国海事贸易运营机构周二表示，一艘货船在经过霍尔木兹海峡时被炮弹击中，这表明随着华盛顿和德黑兰加强立场，该航道上持续存在航行风险。

该海事机构表示，这次袭击造成机舱受损，并导致一名船员伤亡，并补充说，其余船员正在阿曼海岸警卫队的协助下。

这起事件发生在一艘伊朗船只之后。军方官员多次威胁伊斯兰国不会在霍尔木兹海峡问题上让步。福克斯新闻周二报道称，伊朗军方发言人易卜拉欣·佐尔法加里 (Ebrahim Zolfaghari) 表示，试图通过该海峡的船只将“在船体上发现几个漂亮的洞”。

在 6 月中旬达成旨在为外交开放空间的 60 天停火谈判协议后，华盛顿和德黑兰拒绝进一步谈判。欧亚集团的一个分析师团队周一在一份报告中表示，“双方都将陷入更长时间的僵局”，因为双方都认为没有迫切需要做出让步。

周一早些时候，美国唐纳德·特朗普总统排除了延长停火的可能性，称德黑兰不会接受他认为结束战争所必需的条款。特朗普在椭圆形办公室表示，“他们不会达成我认为必要的协议。”

据《华尔街日报》周日援引未透露姓名的伊朗和阿拉伯官员获得的情报报道，伊朗的强硬领导层无意结束冲突，而是扩大战争，增加美国及其地区盟友的成本。

欧亚集团不再期望在随着僵局的持续，将降级时间表推迟到年底。该风险咨询公司表示，最有可能的结果是“达成一项有限的协议”，使霍尔木兹海峡的交通部分恢复，并补充说，华盛顿推动立即重新开放该海峡的压力已经缓解。

欧亚集团表示，霍尔木兹海峡周围石油运输的成功使石油价格不会飙升至每桶100美元以上，而全球经济已经适应了封锁，这给了美国“有能力等待”的空间。

霍尔木兹海峡在战前处理了世界约五分之一的原油和天然气，自二月份以来已成为美国和伊朗之间的主要爆发点。由于油轮遭到零星袭击，航运业仍接近停滞状态。根据 Kpler 的船舶追踪数据，周日只有三艘船只通过霍尔木宗海峡。

据路透社报道，也门胡塞武装于 7 月中旬宣布对沙特阿拉伯实施海上封锁的曼德海峡，周末也只有 49 艘商品船过境，低于前一周的 55 艘。

伊朗外交阿巴斯·阿拉格奇部长周六在电报中表示，伊朗与阿曼的谈判仍在进行中，以确定霍尔木兹海峡的新海上路线，而特朗普周一威胁称，如果阿曼这个海湾国家“妨碍”美国重新开放该海峡的努力，则将轰炸阿曼。

欧亚大陆分析师表示，“霍尔木兹流量的任何恢复都将是部分的”，因为美国和伊朗仍处于紧张状态。敌对行动一触即发，再次爆发冲突、扰乱交通的风险加大。

在 60 天的谈判解决窗口期结束但未取得突破之后，油价攀升。原油期货继周一上涨 2.6% 后，周二上涨 0.25%，至每桶 84.7 美元。

国际基准布伦特原油在周一突破 90 美元后，周二几乎没有变化，最新交易价格为每桶 90.86 美元。
